1CH.28.10.t: Consider now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it.”
s: Consider now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it.”

1CH.28.11.t: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the portico of the temple, its buildings, storehouses, upper rooms, inner rooms, and the room for the mercy seat.
s: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the portico of the temple, its buildings, storehouses, upper rooms, inner rooms, and the room for the mercy seat.

1CH.28.12.t: The plans contained everything David had in mind for the courts of the house of the LORD, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of the house of God and of the dedicated things,
s: The plans contained everything David had in mind for the courts of the house of the LORD, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of the house of God and of the dedicated things,

1CH.28.13.t: for the divisions of the priests and Levites, for all the work of service in the house of the LORD, and for all the articles of service in the house of the LORD:
s: for the divisions of the priests and Levites, for all the work of service in the house of the LORD, and for all the articles of service in the house of the LORD:

1CH.28.14.t: the weight of all the gold articles for every kind of service; the weight of all the silver articles for every kind of service;
s: the weight of all the gold articles for every kind of service;
the weight of all the silver articles for every kind of service;

1CH.28.15.t: the weight of the gold lampstands and their lamps, including the weight of each lampstand and its lamps; the weight of each silver lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;
s: the weight of the gold lampstands and their lamps, including the weight of each lampstand and its lamps;
the weight of each silver lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;

1CH.28.16.t: the weight of gold for each table of showbread, and of silver for the silver tables;
s: the weight of gold for each table of showbread, and of silver for the silver tables;

1CH.28.17.t: the weight of the pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls, and pitchers; the weight of each gold dish; the weight of each silver bowl;
s: the weight of the pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls, and pitchers;
the weight of each gold dish;
the weight of each silver bowl;

1CH.28.18.t: the weight of the refined gold for the altar of incense; and the plans for the chariot of the gold cherubim that spread their wings and overshadowed the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
s: the weight of the refined gold for the altar of incense;
and the plans for the chariot of the gold cherubim that spread their wings and overshadowed the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

1CH.28.19.t: “All this,” said David, “all the details of this plan, the LORD has made clear to me in writing by His hand upon me.”
s: “All this,” said David, “all the details of this plan, the LORD has made clear to me in writing by His hand upon me.”

1CH.28.20.t: David also said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will neither fail you nor forsake you before all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.
s: David also said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will neither fail you nor forsake you before all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

1CH.28.21.t: The divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the service of the house of God, and every willing man of every skill will be at your disposal for the work. The officials and all the people are fully at your command.”
s: The divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the service of the house of God, and every willing man of every skill will be at your disposal for the work. The officials and all the people are fully at your command.”

1CH.29.10.t: Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of all the assembly and said: “May You be blessed, O LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.
s: Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of all the assembly and said:
“May You be blessed, O LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

1CH.29.11.t: Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth belongs to You. Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all.
s: Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth belongs to You.
Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all.

1CH.29.12.t: Both riches and honor come from You, and You are the ruler over all. In Your hands are power and might to exalt and give strength to all.
s: Both riches and honor come from You, and You are the ruler over all. In Your hands are power and might to exalt and give strength to all.

1CH.29.13.t: Now therefore, our God, we give You thanks, and we praise Your glorious name.
s: Now therefore, our God, we give You thanks, and we praise Your glorious name.

1CH.29.14.t: But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? For everything comes from You, and from Your own hand we have given to You.
s: But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? For everything comes from You, and from Your own hand we have given to You.

1CO.4.1.t: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
s: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

1CO.4.2.t: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.
s: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

1CO.4.3.t: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.
s: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.

1CO.4.4.t: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.
s: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.

1CO.4.5.t: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.
s: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.

1CO.7.17.t: Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.
s: Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.

1CO.7.18.t: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.
s: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.

1CO.7.19.t: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.
s: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.

1CO.7.20.t: Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.
s: Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.

1CO.7.21.t: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you—but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
s: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you—but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.

1CO.7.22.t: For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.
s: For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.

1CO.7.23.t: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.
s: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.

1CO.7.24.t: Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him.
s: Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him.

1CO.9.19.t: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
s: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.

1CO.9.20.t: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.
s: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.

1CO.9.21.t: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.
s: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.

1CO.9.22.t: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
s: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.

1CO.9.23.t: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.
s: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.

1CO.9.24.t: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.
s: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.

1CO.9.25.t: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.
s: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.

1CO.9.26.t: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.
s: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.

1CO.9.27.t: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
s: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.

1CO.10.6.t: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.
s: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.

1CO.10.7.t: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”
s: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”

1CO.10.8.t: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
s: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.

1CO.10.9.t: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
s: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.

1CO.10.10.t: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.
s: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.

1CO.10.11.t: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.
s: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

1CO.10.12.t: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.
s: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.

1CO.10.13.t: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
s: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.

1CO.10.14.t: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
s: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

1CO.12.14.t: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.
s: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.

1CO.12.15.t: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
s: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

1CO.12.16.t: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
s: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

1CO.12.17.t: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
s: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?

1CO.12.18.t: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.
s: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.

1CO.12.19.t: If they were all one part, where would the body be?
s: If they were all one part, where would the body be?

1CO.12.20.t: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
s: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

1CO.12.21.t: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”
s: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”

1CO.12.22.t: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
s: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,

1CO.12.23.t: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,
s: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,

1CO.12.24.t: whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,
s: whereas our presentable parts have no such need.
But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,

1CO.12.25.t: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.
s: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.

1CO.12.26.t: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.
s: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.

1CO.12.31.t: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the most excellent way.
s: But eagerly desire the greater gifts.
And now I will show you the most excellent way.

1CO.13.1.t: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.
s: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.

1CO.13.2.t: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
s: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

1CO.13.3.t: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.
s: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.

1CO.13.4.t: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
s: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

1CO.13.5.t: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.
s: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.

1CO.13.6.t: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.
s: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.

1CO.13.7.t: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
s: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

1CO.13.8.t: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.
s: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.

1CO.13.9.t: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
s: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,

1CO.13.10.t: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.
s: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.

1CO.13.11.t: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.
s: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.

1CO.13.12.t: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.
s: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.

1CO.13.13.t: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.
s: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.

1CO.15.55.t: “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?”
s: “Where, O Death, is your victory?
Where, O Death, is your sting?”

1CO.15.56.t: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
s: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

1CO.15.57.t: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
s: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!

1CO.15.58.t: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
s: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

1CO.16.5.t: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.
s: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.

1CO.16.6.t: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
s: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.

1CO.16.7.t: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
s: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.

1CO.16.8.t: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
s: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,

1CO.16.9.t: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.
s: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.

1CO.16.10.t: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.
s: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.

1CO.16.11.t: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.
s: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.

1CO.16.12.t: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.
s: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.

1CO.16.13.t: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
s: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
Do everything in love.

1JN.1.5.t: And this is the message we have heard from Him and announce to you: God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all.
s: And this is the message we have heard from Him and announce to you: God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all.

1JN.1.6.t: If we say we have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
s: If we say we have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.

1JN.1.7.t: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.
s: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.

1JN.1.8.t: If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
s: If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

1JN.1.9.t: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
s: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

1JN.1.10.t: If we say we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.
s: If we say we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.

1JN.2.1.t: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.
s: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.

1JN.2.2.t: He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.
s: He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.

1JN.2.28.t: And now, little children, remain in Christ, so that when He appears, we may be confident and unashamed before Him at His coming.
s: And now, little children, remain in Christ, so that when He appears, we may be confident and unashamed before Him at His coming.

1JN.2.29.t: If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.
s: If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.

1JN.3.1.t: Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know Him.
s: Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know Him.

1JN.3.2.t: Beloved, we are now children of God, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when Christ appears, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is.
s: Beloved, we are now children of God, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when Christ appears, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is.

1JN.3.3.t: And everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself, just as Christ is pure.
s: And everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself, just as Christ is pure.

1JN.3.11.t: This is the message you have heard from the beginning: We should love one another.
s: This is the message you have heard from the beginning: We should love one another.

1JN.3.12.t: Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did Cain slay him? Because his own deeds were evil, while those of his brother were righteous.
s: Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did Cain slay him? Because his own deeds were evil, while those of his brother were righteous.

1JN.3.13.t: So do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.
s: So do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.

1JN.3.14.t: We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.
s: We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.

1JN.3.15.t: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that eternal life does not reside in a murderer.
s: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that eternal life does not reside in a murderer.

1JN.3.16.t: By this we know what love is: Jesus laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.
s: By this we know what love is: Jesus laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.

1JN.3.17.t: If anyone with earthly possessions sees his brother in need, but withholds his compassion from him, how can the love of God abide in him?
s: If anyone with earthly possessions sees his brother in need, but withholds his compassion from him, how can the love of God abide in him?

1JN.3.18.t: Little children, let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth.
s: Little children, let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth.

1JN.3.19.t: And by this we will know that we belong to the truth, and will assure our hearts in His presence:
s: And by this we will know that we belong to the truth, and will assure our hearts in His presence:

1JN.3.20.t: Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things.
s: Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things.

1JN.3.21.t: Beloved, if our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence before God,
s: Beloved, if our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence before God,

1JN.3.22.t: and we will receive from Him whatever we ask, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing in His sight.
s: and we will receive from Him whatever we ask, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing in His sight.

1JN.4.1.t: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God. For many false prophets have gone out into the world.
s: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God. For many false prophets have gone out into the world.

1JN.4.2.t: By this you will know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God,
s: By this you will know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God,

1JN.4.3.t: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time.
s: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time.

1JN.4.4.t: You, little children, are from God and have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world.
s: You, little children, are from God and have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world.

1JN.4.5.t: They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them.
s: They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them.

1JN.4.6.t: We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. That is how we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of deception.
s: We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. That is how we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of deception.

1JN.4.7.t: Beloved, let us love one another, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
s: Beloved, let us love one another, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.

1JN.4.8.t: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
s: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.

1JN.4.9.t: This is how God’s love was revealed among us: God sent His one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.
s: This is how God’s love was revealed among us: God sent His one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.

1JN.4.10.t: And love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
s: And love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

1JN.4.11.t: Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.
s: Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.

1JN.4.12.t: No one has ever seen God; but if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us.
s: No one has ever seen God; but if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us.

1KI.3.5.t: One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream, and God said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”
s: One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream, and God said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”

1KI.3.6.t: Solomon replied, “You have shown much loving devotion to Your servant, my father David, because he walked before You in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. And You have maintained this loving devotion by giving him a son to sit on his throne this very day.
s: Solomon replied, “You have shown much loving devotion to Your servant, my father David, because he walked before You in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. And You have maintained this loving devotion by giving him a son to sit on his throne this very day.

1KI.3.7.t: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in my father David’s place. But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.
s: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in my father David’s place. But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.

1KI.3.8.t: Your servant is here among the people You have chosen, a people too numerous to count or number.
s: Your servant is here among the people You have chosen, a people too numerous to count or number.

1KI.3.9.t: Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”
s: Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”

1KI.3.10.t: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.
s: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.

1KI.3.11.t: So God said to him, “Since you have asked for this instead of requesting long life or wealth for yourself or death for your enemies—but you have asked for discernment to administer justice—
s: So God said to him, “Since you have asked for this instead of requesting long life or wealth for yourself or death for your enemies—but you have asked for discernment to administer justice—

1KI.3.12.t: behold, I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has never been nor will ever be another like you.
s: behold, I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has never been nor will ever be another like you.

1KI.4.29.t: And God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.
s: And God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.

1KI.4.30.t: Solomon’s wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
s: Solomon’s wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.

1KI.4.31.t: He was wiser than all men—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and wiser than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame spread throughout the surrounding nations.
s: He was wiser than all men—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and wiser than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame spread throughout the surrounding nations.

1KI.4.32.t: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
s: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.

1KI.4.33.t: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
s: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.

1KI.4.34.t: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
s: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.

1KI.12.3.t: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
s: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,

1KI.12.4.t: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
s: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”

1KI.12.5.t: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.
s: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.

1KI.12.6.t: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
s: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.

1KI.12.7.t: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
s: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”

1KI.12.8.t: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
s: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.

1KI.12.9.t: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
s: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”

1KI.12.10.t: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
s: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!

1KI.12.11.t: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”
s: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”

1KI.12.12.t: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
s: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”

1KI.12.13.t: And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders
s: And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders

1KI.12.14.t: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
s: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”

1KI.19.3.t: And Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there,
s: And Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there,

1KI.19.4.t: while he himself traveled on a day’s journey into the wilderness. He sat down under a broom tree and prayed that he might die. “I have had enough, LORD,” he said. “Take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.”
s: while he himself traveled on a day’s journey into the wilderness. He sat down under a broom tree and prayed that he might die. “I have had enough, LORD,” he said. “Take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.”

1KI.19.5.t: Then he lay down under the broom tree and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
s: Then he lay down under the broom tree and fell asleep.
Suddenly an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”

1KI.19.6.t: And he looked around, and there by his head was a cake of bread baked over hot coals, and a jar of water. So he ate and drank and lay down again.
s: And he looked around, and there by his head was a cake of bread baked over hot coals, and a jar of water. So he ate and drank and lay down again.

1KI.19.7.t: A second time the angel of the LORD returned and touched him, saying, “Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you.”
s: A second time the angel of the LORD returned and touched him, saying, “Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you.”

1KI.19.8.t: So he got up and ate and drank. And strengthened by that food, he walked forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.
s: So he got up and ate and drank. And strengthened by that food, he walked forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.

1KI.19.9.t: There Elijah entered a cave and spent the night. And the word of the LORD came to him, saying, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
s: There Elijah entered a cave and spent the night. And the word of the LORD came to him, saying, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

1KI.19.10.t: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”
s: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”

1KI.19.11.t: Then the LORD said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD. Behold, the LORD is about to pass by.” And a great and mighty wind tore into the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
s: Then the LORD said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD. Behold, the LORD is about to pass by.”
And a great and mighty wind tore into the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind.
After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.

1KI.19.12.t: After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came a still, small voice.
s: After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire.
And after the fire came a still, small voice.

1KI.19.13.t: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the mouth of the cave. Suddenly a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
s: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the mouth of the cave. Suddenly a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

1KI.19.14.t: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”
s: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”

1KI.19.15.t: Then the LORD said to him, “Go back by the way you came, and go to the Desert of Damascus. When you arrive, you are to anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
s: Then the LORD said to him, “Go back by the way you came, and go to the Desert of Damascus. When you arrive, you are to anoint Hazael as king over Aram.

1KI.19.16.t: You are also to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel and Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah to succeed you as prophet.
s: You are also to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel and Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah to succeed you as prophet.

1KI.19.17.t: Then Jehu will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, and Elisha will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Jehu.
s: Then Jehu will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, and Elisha will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Jehu.

1KI.19.18.t: Nevertheless, I have reserved seven thousand in Israel—all whose knees have not bowed to Baal and whose mouths have not kissed him.”
s: Nevertheless, I have reserved seven thousand in Israel—all whose knees have not bowed to Baal and whose mouths have not kissed him.”

1KI.19.19.t: So Elijah departed and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve teams of oxen, and he was with the twelfth team. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak around him.
s: So Elijah departed and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve teams of oxen, and he was with the twelfth team. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak around him.

1KI.19.20.t: So Elisha left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you.” “Go on back,” Elijah replied, “for what have I done to you?”
s: So Elisha left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you.”
“Go on back,” Elijah replied, “for what have I done to you?”

1KI.19.21.t: So Elisha turned back from him, took his pair of oxen, and slaughtered them. With the oxen’s equipment, he cooked the meat and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out to follow and serve Elijah.
s: So Elisha turned back from him, took his pair of oxen, and slaughtered them. With the oxen’s equipment, he cooked the meat and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out to follow and serve Elijah.

1PE.1.3.t: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! By His great mercy He has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
s: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! By His great mercy He has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

1PE.1.4.t: and into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you,
s: and into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you,

1PE.1.5.t: who through faith are shielded by God’s power for the salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last time.
s: who through faith are shielded by God’s power for the salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last time.

1PE.1.6.t: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials
s: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials

1PE.1.7.t: so that the proven character of your faith—more precious than gold, which perishes even though refined by fire—may result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
s: so that the proven character of your faith—more precious than gold, which perishes even though refined by fire—may result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

1PE.1.8.t: Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy,
s: Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy,

1PE.1.9.t: now that you are receiving the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
s: now that you are receiving the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.

1PE.2.4.t: As you come to Him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight,
s: As you come to Him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight,

1PE.2.5.t: you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
s: you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

1PE.2.6.t: For it stands in Scripture: “See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
s: For it stands in Scripture:
“See, I lay in Zion a stone,
a chosen and precious cornerstone;
and the one who believes in Him
will never be put to shame.”

1PE.2.7.t: To you who believe, then, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe, “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,”
s: To you who believe, then, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe,
“The stone the builders rejected
has become the cornerstone,”

1PE.2.8.t: and, “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.
s: and,
“A stone of stumbling
and a rock of offense.”
They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.

1PE.2.9.t: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
s: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.

1PE.2.10.t: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
s: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

1PE.2.11.t: Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul.
s: Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul.

1PE.2.12.t: Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us.
s: Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us.

1PE.3.8.t: Finally, all of you, be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble.
s: Finally, all of you, be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble.

1PE.3.9.t: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.
s: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.

1PE.3.10.t: For, “Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.
s: For,
“Whoever would love life
and see good days
must keep his tongue from evil
and his lips from deceitful speech.

1PE.3.11.t: He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.
s: He must turn from evil and do good;
he must seek peace and pursue it.

1PE.3.12.t: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
s: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous,
and His ears are inclined to their prayer.
But the face of the Lord is against
those who do evil.”

1PE.4.7.t: The end of all things is near. Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray.
s: The end of all things is near. Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray.

1PE.4.8.t: Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
s: Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.

1PE.4.9.t: Show hospitality to one another without complaining.
s: Show hospitality to one another without complaining.

1PE.4.10.t: As good stewards of the manifold grace of God, each of you should use whatever gift he has received to serve one another.
s: As good stewards of the manifold grace of God, each of you should use whatever gift he has received to serve one another.

1PE.4.11.t: If anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God. If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
s: If anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God. If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.

1PE.5.1.t: As a fellow elder, a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and a partaker of the glory to be revealed, I appeal to the elders among you:
s: As a fellow elder, a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and a partaker of the glory to be revealed, I appeal to the elders among you:

1PE.5.2.t: Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you, watching over them not out of compulsion, but because it is God’s will; not out of greed, but out of eagerness;
s: Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you, watching over them not out of compulsion, but because it is God’s will; not out of greed, but out of eagerness;

1PE.5.3.t: not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.
s: not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.

1PE.5.4.t: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away.
s: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away.

1PE.5.5.t: Young men, in the same way, submit yourselves to your elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
s: Young men, in the same way, submit yourselves to your elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because,
“God opposes the proud,
but gives grace to the humble.”

1PE.5.6.t: Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand, so that in due time He may exalt you.
s: Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand, so that in due time He may exalt you.

1PE.5.7.t: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.
s: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.

1PE.5.8.t: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
s: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.

1PE.5.9.t: Resist him, standing firm in your faith and in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering.
s: Resist him, standing firm in your faith and in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering.

1PE.5.10.t: And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.
s: And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.

1PE.5.11.t: To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen.
s: To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen.

1SA.1.9.t: So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
s: So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

1SA.1.10.t: In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.
s: In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.

1SA.1.11.t: And she made a vow, pleading, “O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son, then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever come over his head.”
s: And she made a vow, pleading, “O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son, then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever come over his head.”

1SA.1.12.t: As Hannah kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.
s: As Hannah kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.

1SA.1.13.t: Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk
s: Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard.
So Eli thought she was drunk

1SA.1.14.t: and said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!”
s: and said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!”

1SA.1.15.t: “No, my lord,” Hannah replied. “I am a woman oppressed in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.
s: “No, my lord,” Hannah replied. “I am a woman oppressed in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.

1SA.1.16.t: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman; for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.”
s: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman; for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.”

1SA.1.17.t: “Go in peace,” Eli replied, “and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.”
s: “Go in peace,” Eli replied, “and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.”

1SA.1.18.t: “May your maidservant find favor with you,” said Hannah. Then she went on her way, and she began eating again, and her face was no longer downcast.
s: “May your maidservant find favor with you,” said Hannah. Then she went on her way, and she began eating again, and her face was no longer downcast.

1SA.1.20.t: So in the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.”
s: So in the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.”

1SA.1.21.t: Then Elkanah and all his house went up to make the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow,
s: Then Elkanah and all his house went up to make the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow,

1SA.1.22.t: but Hannah did not go. “After the boy is weaned,” she said to her husband, “I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.”
s: but Hannah did not go. “After the boy is weaned,” she said to her husband, “I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.”

1SA.1.23.t: “Do what you think is best,” her husband Elkanah replied, “and stay here until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD confirm His word.” So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
s: “Do what you think is best,” her husband Elkanah replied, “and stay here until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD confirm His word.”
So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.

1SA.1.24.t: Once she had weaned him, Hannah took the boy with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.
s: Once she had weaned him, Hannah took the boy with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.

1SA.1.25.t: And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.
s: And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.

1SA.1.26.t: “Please, my lord,” said Hannah, “as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.
s: “Please, my lord,” said Hannah, “as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.

1SA.1.27.t: I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him,
s: I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him,

1SA.1.28.t: I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.” So they worshiped the LORD there.
s: I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.”
So they worshiped the LORD there.

1SA.2.18.t: Now Samuel was ministering before the LORD—a boy wearing a linen ephod.
s: Now Samuel was ministering before the LORD—a boy wearing a linen ephod.

1SA.2.19.t: Each year his mother would make him a little robe and bring it to him when she went with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.
s: Each year his mother would make him a little robe and bring it to him when she went with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.

1SA.2.20.t: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, “May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD.” Then they would go home.
s: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, “May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD.” Then they would go home.

1SA.2.21.t: So the LORD attended to Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.
s: So the LORD attended to Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters.
Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.

1SA.3.1.t: And the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli. Now in those days the word of the LORD was rare and visions were scarce.
s: And the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli.
Now in those days the word of the LORD was rare and visions were scarce.

1SA.3.2.t: And at that time Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see, was lying in his room.
s: And at that time Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see, was lying in his room.

1SA.3.3.t: Before the lamp of God had gone out, Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.
s: Before the lamp of God had gone out, Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.

1SA.3.4.t: Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, “Here I am.”
s: Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, “Here I am.”

1SA.3.5.t: He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.” “I did not call,” Eli replied. “Go back and lie down.” So he went and lay down.
s: He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”
“I did not call,” Eli replied. “Go back and lie down.”
So he went and lay down.

1SA.3.6.t: Once again the LORD called, “Samuel!” So Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.” “My son, I did not call,” Eli replied. “Go back and lie down.”
s: Once again the LORD called, “Samuel!”
So Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”
“My son, I did not call,” Eli replied. “Go back and lie down.”

1SA.3.7.t: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, because the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
s: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, because the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.

1SA.3.8.t: Once again, for the third time, the LORD called to Samuel. He got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.” Then Eli realized that it was the LORD who was calling the boy.
s: Once again, for the third time, the LORD called to Samuel. He got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”
Then Eli realized that it was the LORD who was calling the boy.

1SA.3.9.t: “Go and lie down,” he said to Samuel, “and if He calls you, say, ‘Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
s: “Go and lie down,” he said to Samuel, “and if He calls you, say, ‘Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.’”
So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

1SA.3.10.t: Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel answered, “Speak, for Your servant is listening.”
s: Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!”
And Samuel answered, “Speak, for Your servant is listening.”

1SA.12.1.t: Then Samuel said to all Israel, “I have listened to your voice in all that you have said to me, and I have set over you a king.
s: Then Samuel said to all Israel, “I have listened to your voice in all that you have said to me, and I have set over you a king.

1SA.12.2.t: Now here is the king walking before you, and I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.
s: Now here is the king walking before you, and I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

1SA.12.3.t: Here I am. Bear witness against me before the LORD and before His anointed: Whose ox or donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated or oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe and closed my eyes? Tell me, and I will restore it to you.”
s: Here I am. Bear witness against me before the LORD and before His anointed: Whose ox or donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated or oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe and closed my eyes? Tell me, and I will restore it to you.”

1SA.12.4.t: “You have not wronged us or oppressed us,” they replied, “nor have you taken anything from the hand of man.”
s: “You have not wronged us or oppressed us,” they replied, “nor have you taken anything from the hand of man.”

1SA.12.5.t: Samuel said to them, “The LORD is a witness against you, and His anointed is a witness today, that you have not found anything in my hand.” “He is a witness,” they replied.
s: Samuel said to them, “The LORD is a witness against you, and His anointed is a witness today, that you have not found anything in my hand.”
“He is a witness,” they replied.

1SA.12.19.t: They pleaded with Samuel, “Pray to the LORD your God for your servants so that we will not die! For we have added to all our sins the evil of asking for a king.”
s: They pleaded with Samuel, “Pray to the LORD your God for your servants so that we will not die! For we have added to all our sins the evil of asking for a king.”

1SA.12.20.t: “Do not be afraid,” Samuel replied. “Even though you have committed all this evil, do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
s: “Do not be afraid,” Samuel replied. “Even though you have committed all this evil, do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.

1SA.12.21.t: Do not turn aside after worthless things that cannot profit you or deliver you, for they are empty.
s: Do not turn aside after worthless things that cannot profit you or deliver you, for they are empty.

1SA.12.22.t: Indeed, for the sake of His great name, the LORD will not abandon His people, because He was pleased to make you His own.
s: Indeed, for the sake of His great name, the LORD will not abandon His people, because He was pleased to make you His own.

1SA.12.23.t: As for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. And I will continue to teach you the good and right way.
s: As for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. And I will continue to teach you the good and right way.

1SA.12.24.t: Above all, fear the LORD and serve Him faithfully with all your heart; consider what great things He has done for you.
s: Above all, fear the LORD and serve Him faithfully with all your heart; consider what great things He has done for you.

1SA.12.25.t: But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”
s: But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”

1SA.16.1.t: Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.”
s: Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.”

1SA.16.2.t: “How can I go?” Samuel asked. “Saul will hear of it and kill me!” The LORD answered, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’
s: “How can I go?” Samuel asked. “Saul will hear of it and kill me!”
The LORD answered, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’

1SA.16.3.t: Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do. You are to anoint for Me the one I indicate.”
s: Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do. You are to anoint for Me the one I indicate.”

1SA.16.4.t: So Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. When the elders of the town met him, they trembled and asked, “Do you come in peace?”
s: So Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. When the elders of the town met him, they trembled and asked, “Do you come in peace?”

1SA.16.5.t: “In peace,” he replied. “I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.” Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
s: “In peace,” he replied. “I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.”
Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

1SA.16.6.t: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and said, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.”
s: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and said, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.”

1SA.16.7.t: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.”
s: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.”

1SA.16.8.t: Then Jesse called Abinadab and presented him to Samuel, who said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
s: Then Jesse called Abinadab and presented him to Samuel, who said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”

1SA.16.9.t: Next Jesse presented Shammah, but Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
s: Next Jesse presented Shammah, but Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”

1SA.16.10.t: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel told him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”
s: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel told him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”

1SA.16.11.t: And Samuel asked him, “Are these all the sons you have?” “There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.” “Send for him,” Samuel replied. “For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.”
s: And Samuel asked him, “Are these all the sons you have?”
“There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.”
“Send for him,” Samuel replied. “For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.”

1SA.16.12.t: So Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.”
s: So Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.”

1SA.16.13.t: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah.
s: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah.

1SA.17.32.t: And David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!”
s: And David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!”

1SA.17.33.t: But Saul replied, “You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”
s: But Saul replied, “You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”

1SA.17.34.t: David replied, “Your servant has been tending his father’s sheep, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock,
s: David replied, “Your servant has been tending his father’s sheep, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock,

1SA.17.35.t: I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.
s: I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.

1SA.17.36.t: Your servant has killed lions and bears; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God.”
s: Your servant has killed lions and bears; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God.”

1SA.17.37.t: David added, “The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.” “Go,” said Saul, “and may the LORD be with you.”
s: David added, “The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.”
“Go,” said Saul, “and may the LORD be with you.”

1SA.17.38.t: Then Saul clothed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor.
s: Then Saul clothed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor.

1SA.17.39.t: David strapped his sword over the tunic and tried to walk, but he was not accustomed to them. “I cannot walk in these,” David said to Saul. “I am not accustomed to them.” So David took them off.
s: David strapped his sword over the tunic and tried to walk, but he was not accustomed to them.
“I cannot walk in these,” David said to Saul. “I am not accustomed to them.” So David took them off.

1SA.17.40.t: And David took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag. And with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.
s: And David took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag. And with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.

1SA.19.1.t: Then Saul ordered his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. But Jonathan delighted greatly in David,
s: Then Saul ordered his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David.
But Jonathan delighted greatly in David,

1SA.19.2.t: so he warned David, saying, “My father Saul intends to kill you. Be on your guard in the morning; find a secret place and hide there.
s: so he warned David, saying, “My father Saul intends to kill you. Be on your guard in the morning; find a secret place and hide there.

1SA.19.3.t: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, so I can ask about you. And if I find out anything, I will tell you.”
s: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, so I can ask about you. And if I find out anything, I will tell you.”

1SA.19.4.t: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, “The king should not sin against his servant David; he has not sinned against you. In fact, his actions have been highly beneficial to you.
s: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, “The king should not sin against his servant David; he has not sinned against you. In fact, his actions have been highly beneficial to you.

1SA.19.5.t: He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced, so why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?”
s: He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced, so why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?”

1SA.19.6.t: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan and swore an oath: “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.”
s: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan and swore an oath: “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.”

1SA.19.7.t: So Jonathan summoned David and told him all these things. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul to serve him as he had before.
s: So Jonathan summoned David and told him all these things. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul to serve him as he had before.

1SA.23.14.t: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.
s: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.

1SA.23.15.t: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.
s: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.

1SA.23.16.t: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,
s: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,

1SA.23.17.t: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”
s: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”

1SA.23.18.t: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.
s: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.

1SA.24.1.t: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”
s: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”
