1SA.24.2.t: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
s: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

1SA.24.3.t: Soon Saul came to the sheepfolds along the road, where there was a cave, and he went in to relieve himself. And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.
s: Soon Saul came to the sheepfolds along the road, where there was a cave, and he went in to relieve himself. And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.

1SA.24.4.t: So David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do with him as you wish.’” Then David crept up secretly and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.
s: So David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do with him as you wish.’”
Then David crept up secretly and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.

1SA.24.5.t: Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.
s: Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.

1SA.24.6.t: So he said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed. May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
s: So he said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed. May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”

1SA.24.7.t: With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and went on his way.
s: With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and went on his way.

1SA.24.8.t: After that, David got up, went out of the cave, and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!” When Saul looked behind him, David bowed facedown in reverence
s: After that, David got up, went out of the cave, and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!”
When Saul looked behind him, David bowed facedown in reverence

1SA.24.9.t: and said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’?
s: and said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’?

1SA.24.10.t: Behold, this day you have seen with your own eyes that the LORD delivered you into my hand in the cave. I was told to kill you, but I spared you and said, ‘I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed.’
s: Behold, this day you have seen with your own eyes that the LORD delivered you into my hand in the cave. I was told to kill you, but I spared you and said, ‘I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed.’

1SA.25.23.t: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him.
s: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him.

1SA.25.24.t: She fell at his feet and said, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.
s: She fell at his feet and said, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.

1SA.25.25.t: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him. I, your servant, did not see my lord’s young men whom you sent.
s: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him. I, your servant, did not see my lord’s young men whom you sent.

1SA.25.26.t: Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, the LORD has held you back from coming to bloodshed and avenging yourself with your own hand. May your enemies and those who seek harm for my lord be like Nabal.
s: Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, the LORD has held you back from coming to bloodshed and avenging yourself with your own hand. May your enemies and those who seek harm for my lord be like Nabal.

1SA.25.27.t: Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.
s: Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.

1SA.25.28.t: Please forgive your servant’s offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles. May no evil be found in you as long as you live.
s: Please forgive your servant’s offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles. May no evil be found in you as long as you live.

1SA.25.29.t: And should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living. But He shall fling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.
s: And should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living. But He shall fling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.

1SA.25.30.t: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good He promised, and when He has appointed you ruler over Israel,
s: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good He promised, and when He has appointed you ruler over Israel,

1SA.25.31.t: then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your maidservant.”
s: then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your maidservant.”

1SA.25.32.t: Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!
s: Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!

1SA.25.33.t: Blessed is your discernment, and blessed are you, because today you kept me from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.
s: Blessed is your discernment, and blessed are you, because today you kept me from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.

1SA.25.34.t: Otherwise, as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, then surely no male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by morning light.”
s: Otherwise, as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, then surely no male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by morning light.”

1SA.25.35.t: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, “Go home in peace. See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.”
s: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, “Go home in peace. See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.”

1TH.2.5.t: As you know, we never used words of flattery or any pretext for greed. God is our witness!
s: As you know, we never used words of flattery or any pretext for greed. God is our witness!

1TH.2.6.t: Nor did we seek praise from you or from anyone else, although as apostles of Christ we had authority to demand it.
s: Nor did we seek praise from you or from anyone else, although as apostles of Christ we had authority to demand it.

1TH.2.7.t: On the contrary, we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children.
s: On the contrary, we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children.

1TH.2.8.t: We cared so deeply that we were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God, but our own lives as well. That is how beloved you have become to us.
s: We cared so deeply that we were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God, but our own lives as well. That is how beloved you have become to us.

1TH.2.9.t: Surely you recall, brothers, our labor and toil. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
s: Surely you recall, brothers, our labor and toil. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.

1TH.2.17.t: Brothers, although we were torn away from you for a short time (in person, not in heart), our desire to see you face to face was even more intense.
s: Brothers, although we were torn away from you for a short time (in person, not in heart), our desire to see you face to face was even more intense.

1TH.2.18.t: For we wanted to come to you—indeed I, Paul, tried again and again—but Satan obstructed us.
s: For we wanted to come to you—indeed I, Paul, tried again and again—but Satan obstructed us.

1TH.2.19.t: After all, who is our hope, our joy, our crown of boasting, if it is not you yourselves in the presence of our Lord Jesus at His coming?
s: After all, who is our hope, our joy, our crown of boasting, if it is not you yourselves in the presence of our Lord Jesus at His coming?

1TH.2.20.t: You are indeed our glory and our joy.
s: You are indeed our glory and our joy.

1TH.4.9.t: Now about brotherly love, you do not need anyone to write to you, because you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another.
s: Now about brotherly love, you do not need anyone to write to you, because you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another.

1TH.4.10.t: And you are indeed showing this love to all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to excel more and more
s: And you are indeed showing this love to all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to excel more and more

1TH.4.11.t: and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.
s: and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.

1TH.4.12.t: Then you will behave properly toward outsiders, without being dependent on anyone.
s: Then you will behave properly toward outsiders, without being dependent on anyone.

1TH.5.11.t: Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.
s: Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.

1TH.5.12.t: But we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who preside over you in the Lord and give you instruction.
s: But we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who preside over you in the Lord and give you instruction.

1TH.5.13.t: In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another.
s: In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another.

1TH.5.14.t: And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
s: And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.

1TH.5.15.t: Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
s: Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
Rejoice at all times.
Pray without ceasing.

1TH.5.18.t: Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.
s: Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.
Do not extinguish the Spirit.

1TH.5.20.t: Do not treat prophecies with contempt,
s: Do not treat prophecies with contempt,

1TH.5.21.t: but test all things. Hold fast to what is good.
s: but test all things. Hold fast to what is good.

1TH.5.22.t: Abstain from every form of evil.
s: Abstain from every form of evil.

1TH.5.23.t: Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you completely, and may your entire spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
s: Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you completely, and may your entire spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

1TH.5.24.t: The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.
s: The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.

1TI.4.6.t: By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.
s: By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.

1TI.4.7.t: But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.
s: But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.

1TI.4.8.t: For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.
s: For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.

1TI.4.9.t: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.
s: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.

1TI.4.10.t: To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
s: To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
Command and teach these things.

1TI.4.12.t: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
s: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

1TI.4.13.t: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.
s: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.

1TI.4.14.t: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.
s: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.

1TI.4.15.t: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
s: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.

1TI.4.16.t: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
s: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

2CH.20.5.t: Then Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem in the house of the LORD in front of the new courtyard
s: Then Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem in the house of the LORD in front of the new courtyard

2CH.20.6.t: and said, “O LORD, God of our fathers, are You not the God who is in heaven, and do You not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in Your hand, and no one can stand against You.
s: and said, “O LORD, God of our fathers, are You not the God who is in heaven, and do You not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in Your hand, and no one can stand against You.

2CH.20.7.t: Our God, did You not drive out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham Your friend?
s: Our God, did You not drive out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham Your friend?

2CH.20.8.t: They have lived in the land and have built in it a sanctuary for Your Name, saying,
s: They have lived in the land and have built in it a sanctuary for Your Name, saying,

2CH.20.9.t: ‘If disaster comes upon us—whether sword or judgment, plague or famine—we will stand before this temple and before You, for Your Name is in this temple. We will cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear us and save us.’
s: ‘If disaster comes upon us—whether sword or judgment, plague or famine—we will stand before this temple and before You, for Your Name is in this temple. We will cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear us and save us.’

2CH.20.10.t: And now, here are the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, whom You did not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt; but Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them.
s: And now, here are the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, whom You did not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt; but Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them.

2CH.20.11.t: See how they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of the possession that You gave us as an inheritance.
s: See how they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of the possession that You gave us as an inheritance.

2CH.20.12.t: Our God, will You not judge them? For we are powerless before this vast army that comes against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”
s: Our God, will You not judge them? For we are powerless before this vast army that comes against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”

2CO.1.3.t: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,
s: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,

2CO.1.4.t: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.
s: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.

2CO.1.5.t: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
s: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.

2CO.1.6.t: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.
s: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.

2CO.1.7.t: And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.
s: And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.

2CO.1.8.t: We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.
s: We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.

2CO.1.9.t: Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
s: Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.

2CO.1.10.t: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us,
s: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us,

2CO.1.11.t: as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers.
s: as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers.

2CO.2.5.t: Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you—to some degree, not to overstate it.
s: Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you—to some degree, not to overstate it.

2CO.2.6.t: The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.
s: The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.

2CO.2.7.t: So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
s: So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.

2CO.2.8.t: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
s: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.

2CO.2.9.t: My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.
s: My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.

2CO.2.10.t: If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
s: If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,

2CO.2.11.t: in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.
s: in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.

2CO.3.1.t: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
s: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

2CO.3.2.t: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
s: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

2CO.3.3.t: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
s: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

2CO.3.4.t: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.
s: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.

2CO.3.5.t: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.
s: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.

2CO.3.6.t: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
s: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

2CO.4.6.t: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
s: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

2CO.4.7.t: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.
s: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.

2CO.4.8.t: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
s: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;

2CO.4.9.t: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.
s: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.

2CO.4.10.t: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
s: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

2CO.4.11.t: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.
s: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.

2CO.4.12.t: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
s: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.

2CO.4.13.t: And in keeping with what is written: “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,
s: And in keeping with what is written: “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,

2CO.4.14.t: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.
s: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.

2CO.4.15.t: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may overflow in thanksgiving, to the glory of God.
s: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may overflow in thanksgiving, to the glory of God.

2CO.4.16.t: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
s: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.

2CO.4.17.t: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal glory that is far beyond comparison.
s: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal glory that is far beyond comparison.

2CO.4.18.t: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
s: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.

2CO.6.4.t: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;
s: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;

2CO.6.5.t: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;
s: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;

2CO.6.6.t: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;
s: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;

2CO.6.7.t: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
s: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;

2CO.6.8.t: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;
s: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;

2CO.6.9.t: as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;
s: as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;

2CO.6.10.t: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
s: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.

2CO.7.5.t: For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction—conflicts on the outside, fears within.
s: For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction—conflicts on the outside, fears within.

2CO.7.6.t: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,
s: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,

2CO.7.7.t: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.
s: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.

2CO.12.7.t: or because of these surpassingly great revelations. So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.
s: or because of these surpassingly great revelations.
So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.

2CO.12.8.t: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.
s: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.

2CO.12.9.t: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
s: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.

2CO.12.10.t: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
s: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.

2KI.4.8.t: One day Elisha went to Shunem, and a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal. So whenever he would pass by, he would stop there to eat.
s: One day Elisha went to Shunem, and a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal. So whenever he would pass by, he would stop there to eat.

2KI.4.9.t: Then the woman said to her husband, “Behold, now I know that the one who often comes our way is a holy man of God.
s: Then the woman said to her husband, “Behold, now I know that the one who often comes our way is a holy man of God.

2KI.4.10.t: Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him. Then when he comes to us, he can stay there.”
s: Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him. Then when he comes to us, he can stay there.”

2KI.4.11.t: One day Elisha came to visit and went to his upper room to lie down.
s: One day Elisha came to visit and went to his upper room to lie down.

2KI.5.9.t: So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha’s house.
s: So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha’s house.

2KI.5.10.t: Then Elisha sent him a messenger, who said, “Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.”
s: Then Elisha sent him a messenger, who said, “Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.”

2KI.5.11.t: But Naaman went away angry, saying, “I thought that he would surely come out, stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the spot to cure my leprosy.
s: But Naaman went away angry, saying, “I thought that he would surely come out, stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the spot to cure my leprosy.

2KI.5.12.t: Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not have washed in them and been cleansed?” So he turned and went away in a rage.
s: Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not have washed in them and been cleansed?” So he turned and went away in a rage.

2KI.5.13.t: Naaman’s servants, however, approached him and said, “My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, ‘Wash and be cleansed’?”
s: Naaman’s servants, however, approached him and said, “My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, ‘Wash and be cleansed’?”

2KI.5.14.t: So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child, and he was clean.
s: So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child, and he was clean.

2KI.6.14.t: the king of Aram sent horses, chariots, and a great army. They went there by night and surrounded the city.
s: the king of Aram sent horses, chariots, and a great army. They went there by night and surrounded the city.

2KI.6.15.t: When the servant of the man of God got up and went out early in the morning, an army with horses and chariots had surrounded the city. So he asked Elisha, “Oh, my master, what are we to do?”
s: When the servant of the man of God got up and went out early in the morning, an army with horses and chariots had surrounded the city. So he asked Elisha, “Oh, my master, what are we to do?”

2KI.6.16.t: “Do not be afraid,” Elisha answered, “for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”
s: “Do not be afraid,” Elisha answered, “for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”

2KI.6.17.t: Then Elisha prayed, “O LORD, please open his eyes that he may see.” And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw that the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
s: Then Elisha prayed, “O LORD, please open his eyes that he may see.”
And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw that the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

2KI.6.18.t: As the Arameans came down against him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, “Please strike these people with blindness.” So He struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha.
s: As the Arameans came down against him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, “Please strike these people with blindness.” So He struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha.

2KI.12.9.t: Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD. There the priests who guarded the threshold put all the money brought into the house of the LORD.
s: Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD. There the priests who guarded the threshold put all the money brought into the house of the LORD.

2KI.12.10.t: Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the royal scribe and the high priest would go up, count the money brought into the house of the LORD, and tie it up in bags.
s: Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the royal scribe and the high priest would go up, count the money brought into the house of the LORD, and tie it up in bags.

2KI.12.11.t: Then they would put the counted money into the hands of those who supervised the work on the house of the LORD, who in turn would pay those doing the work—the carpenters, builders,
s: Then they would put the counted money into the hands of those who supervised the work on the house of the LORD, who in turn would pay those doing the work—the carpenters, builders,

2KI.12.12.t: masons, and stonecutters. They also purchased timber and dressed stone to repair the damage to the house of the LORD, and they paid the other expenses of the temple repairs.
s: masons, and stonecutters. They also purchased timber and dressed stone to repair the damage to the house of the LORD, and they paid the other expenses of the temple repairs.

2KI.12.13.t: However, the money brought into the house of the LORD was not used for making silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any articles of gold or silver for the house of the LORD.
s: However, the money brought into the house of the LORD was not used for making silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any articles of gold or silver for the house of the LORD.

2KI.12.14.t: Instead, it was paid to those doing the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
s: Instead, it was paid to those doing the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.

2KI.12.15.t: No accounting was required from the men who received the money to pay the workmen, because they acted with integrity.
s: No accounting was required from the men who received the money to pay the workmen, because they acted with integrity.

2PE.1.3.t: His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.
s: His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.

2PE.1.4.t: Through these He has given us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.
s: Through these He has given us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.

2PE.1.5.t: For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;
s: For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;

2PE.1.6.t: and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness;
s: and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness;

2PE.1.7.t: and to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.
s: and to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.

2PE.1.8.t: For if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
s: For if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

2SA.1.17.t: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,
s: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,

2SA.1.18.t: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:
s: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:

2SA.1.19.t: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
s: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights.
How the mighty have fallen!

2SA.1.20.t: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
s: Tell it not in Gath;
proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon,
lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice,
and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

2SA.1.21.t: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
s: O mountains of Gilboa,
may you have no dew or rain,
no fields yielding offerings of grain.
For there the shield of the mighty was defiled,
the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

2SA.1.22.t: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
s: From the blood of the slain,
from the fat of the mighty,
the bow of Jonathan did not retreat,
and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

2SA.1.23.t: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
s: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life,
were not divided in death.
They were swifter than eagles,
they were stronger than lions.

2SA.1.24.t: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.
s: O daughters of Israel,
weep for Saul,
who clothed you in scarlet and luxury,
who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.

2SA.1.25.t: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
s: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle!
Jonathan lies slain on your heights.

2SA.1.26.t: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
s: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother.
You were delightful to me;
your love to me was extraordinary,
surpassing the love of women.

2SA.1.27.t: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”
s: How the mighty have fallen
and the weapons of war have perished!”

2SA.9.1.t: Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”
s: Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”

2SA.9.2.t: And there was a servant of Saul’s family named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?” “I am your servant,” he replied.
s: And there was a servant of Saul’s family named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?”
“I am your servant,” he replied.

2SA.9.3.t: So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of Saul’s family to whom I can show the kindness of God?” Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”
s: So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of Saul’s family to whom I can show the kindness of God?”
Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”

2SA.9.4.t: “Where is he?” replied the king. And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”
s: “Where is he?” replied the king.
And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”

2SA.9.5.t: So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.
s: So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.

2SA.9.6.t: And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence. Then David said, “Mephibosheth!” “I am your servant,” he replied.
s: And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence.
Then David said, “Mephibosheth!”
“I am your servant,” he replied.

2SA.9.7.t: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”
s: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”

2SA.9.8.t: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”
s: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”

2SA.9.9.t: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.
s: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.

2SA.9.10.t: You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
s: You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.”
Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

2SA.9.11.t: And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.” So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s own sons.
s: And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.”
So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s own sons.

2SA.9.12.t: And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.
s: And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.

2SA.9.13.t: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.
s: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.

2SA.23.1.t: These are the last words of David: “The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:
s: These are the last words of David:
“The oracle of David son of Jesse,
the oracle of the man raised on high,
the one anointed by the God of Jacob,
and the sweet psalmist of Israel:

2SA.23.2.t: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.
s: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me;
His word was on my tongue.

2SA.23.3.t: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, ‘He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,
s: The God of Israel spoke;
the Rock of Israel said to me,
‘He who rules the people with justice,
who rules in the fear of God,

2SA.23.4.t: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn, the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.’
s: is like the light of the morning
at sunrise of a cloudless dawn,
the glistening after the rain
on the sprouting grass of the earth.’

2SA.23.5.t: Is not my house right with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?
s: Is not my house right with God?
For He has established with me
an everlasting covenant,
ordered and secured in every part.
Will He not bring about my full salvation
and my every desire?

2TH.3.16.t: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
s: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.

2TH.3.17.t: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. This is my mark in every letter; it is the way I write.
s: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. This is my mark in every letter; it is the way I write.

2TH.3.18.t: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.
s: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.

2TI.1.3.t: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as did my forefathers, as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers.
s: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as did my forefathers, as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers.

2TI.1.4.t: Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.
s: Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.

2TI.1.5.t: I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced is in you as well.
s: I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced is in you as well.

2TI.1.6.t: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
s: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.

2TI.1.7.t: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
s: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.

2TI.1.8.t: So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God.
s: So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God.

2TI.2.1.t: You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
s: You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.

2TI.2.2.t: And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.
s: And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.

2TI.2.3.t: Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
s: Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

2TI.2.4.t: A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.
s: A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.

2TI.2.5.t: Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.
s: Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.

2TI.2.6.t: The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.
s: The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.

2TI.2.7.t: Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.
s: Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.

2TI.2.8.t: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel,
s: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel,

2TI.2.9.t: for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!
s: for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!

2TI.2.10.t: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
s: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.

2TI.2.11.t: This is a trustworthy saying: If we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
s: This is a trustworthy saying:
If we died with Him,
we will also live with Him;

2TI.2.12.t: if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;
s: if we endure,
we will also reign with Him;
if we deny Him,
He will also deny us;

2TI.2.13.t: if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
s: if we are faithless,
He remains faithful,
for He cannot deny Himself.

2TI.2.14.t: Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.
s: Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.

2TI.2.15.t: Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.
s: Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.

2TI.2.16.t: But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,
s: But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,

2TI.2.17.t: and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
s: and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,

2TI.2.18.t: who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.
s: who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.

2TI.2.19.t: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”
s: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”

2TI.2.20.t: A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
s: A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.

2TI.2.21.t: So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.
s: So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.

2TI.2.22.t: Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
s: Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

2TI.2.23.t: But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.
s: But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.

2TI.2.24.t: And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.
s: And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.

2TI.2.25.t: He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.
s: He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.

2TI.2.26.t: Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.
s: Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.

2TI.3.10.t: You, however, have observed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my perseverance,
s: You, however, have observed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my perseverance,

2TI.3.11.t: my persecutions, and the sufferings that came upon me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet the Lord rescued me from all of them.
s: my persecutions, and the sufferings that came upon me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet the Lord rescued me from all of them.

2TI.3.12.t: Indeed, all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted,
s: Indeed, all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted,

2TI.3.13.t: while evil men and imposters go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
s: while evil men and imposters go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.

2TI.3.14.t: But as for you, continue in the things you have learned and firmly believed, since you know from whom you have learned them.
s: But as for you, continue in the things you have learned and firmly believed, since you know from whom you have learned them.

2TI.3.15.t: From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
s: From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.

2TI.3.16.t: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
s: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness,

2TI.3.17.t: so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
s: so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.

2TI.4.9.t: Make every effort to come to me quickly,
s: Make every effort to come to me quickly,

2TI.4.10.t: because Demas, in his love of this world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
s: because Demas, in his love of this world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.

2TI.4.11.t: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is useful to me in the ministry.
s: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is useful to me in the ministry.

2TI.4.12.t: Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus.
s: Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus.

2TI.4.13.t: When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.
s: When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.

2TI.4.14.t: Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to me. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
s: Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to me. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.

2TI.4.15.t: You too should beware of him, for he has vigorously opposed our message.
s: You too should beware of him, for he has vigorously opposed our message.

2TI.4.16.t: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.
s: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.

2TI.4.17.t: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.
s: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.

2TI.4.18.t: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
s: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

3JN.1.1.t: The elder, To the beloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth:
s: The elder,
To the beloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth:

3JN.1.2.t: Beloved, I pray that in every way you may prosper and enjoy good health, as your soul also prospers.
s: Beloved, I pray that in every way you may prosper and enjoy good health, as your soul also prospers.

3JN.1.3.t: For I was overjoyed when the brothers came and testified about your devotion to the truth, in which you continue to walk.
s: For I was overjoyed when the brothers came and testified about your devotion to the truth, in which you continue to walk.

3JN.1.4.t: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
s: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.

3JN.1.5.t: Beloved, you are faithful in what you are doing for the brothers, and especially since they are strangers to you.
s: Beloved, you are faithful in what you are doing for the brothers, and especially since they are strangers to you.

3JN.1.6.t: They have testified to the church about your love. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.
s: They have testified to the church about your love. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.

3JN.1.7.t: For they went out on behalf of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles.
s: For they went out on behalf of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles.

3JN.1.8.t: Therefore we ought to support such men, so that we may be fellow workers for the truth.
s: Therefore we ought to support such men, so that we may be fellow workers for the truth.

ACT.8.26.t: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”
s: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”

ACT.8.27.t: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,
s: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,

ACT.8.28.t: and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.
s: and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.

ACT.8.29.t: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”
s: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”

ACT.8.30.t: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.
s: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.

ACT.8.31.t: “How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
s: “How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

ACT.8.32.t: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
s: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture:
“He was led like a sheep to the slaughter,
and as a lamb before the shearer is silent,
so He did not open His mouth.

ACT.8.33.t: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth.”
s: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice.
Who can recount His descendants?
For His life was removed from the earth.”

ACT.8.34.t: “Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”
s: “Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”

ACT.8.35.t: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
s: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.

ACT.9.23.t: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,
s: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,

ACT.9.24.t: but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.
s: but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.

ACT.9.25.t: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.
s: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.

ACT.9.26.t: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
s: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

ACT.9.27.t: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.
s: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.

ACT.9.28.t: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
s: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

ACT.9.36.t: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which is translated as Dorcas), who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.
s: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which is translated as Dorcas), who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.

ACT.9.37.t: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.
s: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.

ACT.9.38.t: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him, “Come to us without delay.”
s: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him, “Come to us without delay.”

ACT.9.39.t: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
s: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.

ACT.13.32.t: And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers
s: And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers

ACT.13.33.t: He has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’
s: He has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm:
‘You are My Son;
today I have become Your Father.’

ACT.13.34.t: In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’
s: In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said:
‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’

ACT.13.35.t: So also, He says in another Psalm: ‘You will not let Your Holy One see decay.’
s: So also, He says in another Psalm:
‘You will not let Your Holy One see decay.’

ACT.13.36.t: For when David had served God’s purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.
s: For when David had served God’s purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.

ACT.13.37.t: But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.
s: But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.

ACT.15.36.t: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
s: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”

ACT.15.37.t: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.
s: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.

ACT.15.38.t: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.
s: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.

ACT.15.39.t: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
s: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,

ACT.15.40.t: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
s: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.

ACT.15.41.t: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
s: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

ACT.16.6.t: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.
s: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.

ACT.16.7.t: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.
s: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.

ACT.16.8.t: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
s: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

ACT.16.9.t: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
s: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”

ACT.16.10.t: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
s: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.

ACT.17.10.t: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
s: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

ACT.17.11.t: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
s: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.

ACT.17.12.t: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
s: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.

ACT.17.24.t: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.
s: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.

ACT.17.25.t: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.
s: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

ACT.17.26.t: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
s: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.

ACT.17.27.t: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
s: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.

ACT.17.28.t: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’
s: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’

ACT.18.5.t: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
s: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

ACT.18.6.t: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
s: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”

ACT.18.7.t: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.
s: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.

ACT.18.8.t: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.
s: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.

ACT.18.9.t: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.
s: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.

ACT.18.10.t: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”
s: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”

ACT.18.11.t: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
s: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.

ACT.18.24.t: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
s: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.

ACT.18.25.t: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
s: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.

ACT.18.26.t: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
s: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

ACT.18.27.t: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.
s: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.

ACT.18.28.t: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
s: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

ACT.20.17.t: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.
s: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.

ACT.20.18.t: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.
s: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.

ACT.20.19.t: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
s: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.

ACT.20.20.t: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,
s: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,

ACT.20.21.t: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
s: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.

ACT.20.22.t: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.
s: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.

ACT.20.23.t: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.
s: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.

ACT.20.24.t: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.
s: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.

ACT.20.32.t: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
s: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.

ACT.20.33.t: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.
s: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.

ACT.20.34.t: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.
s: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.

ACT.20.35.t: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
s: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

ACT.20.36.t: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
s: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

ACT.20.37.t: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.
s: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.

ACT.20.38.t: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
s: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

ACT.21.1.t: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
s: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

ACT.21.2.t: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.
s: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.
