ACT.21.3.t: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.
s: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

ACT.21.4.t: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
s: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

ACT.21.5.t: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.
s: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.

ACT.21.6.t: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.
s: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.

ACT.23.12.t: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
s: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

ACT.23.13.t: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.
s: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.

ACT.23.14.t: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
s: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.

ACT.23.15.t: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”
s: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”

ACT.23.16.t: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
s: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.

ACT.23.17.t: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”
s: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”

ACT.23.18.t: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
s: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”

ACT.23.19.t: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”
s: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”

ACT.23.20.t: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.
s: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.

ACT.23.21.t: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”
s: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”

ACT.23.22.t: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”
s: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”

ACT.28.1.t: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
s: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

ACT.28.2.t: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
s: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.

ACT.28.3.t: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
s: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.

ACT.28.4.t: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
s: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”

ACT.28.5.t: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
s: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

ACT.28.6.t: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
s: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

ACT.28.7.t: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
s: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.

ACT.28.8.t: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
s: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.

ACT.28.9.t: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
s: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.

ACT.28.10.t: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.
s: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.

ACT.28.11.t: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
s: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.

ACT.28.12.t: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
s: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

ACT.28.13.t: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
s: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.

ACT.28.14.t: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
s: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.

ACT.28.15.t: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.
s: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

ACT.28.16.t: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
s: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

AMO.7.10.t: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words,
s: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words,

AMO.7.11.t: for this is what Amos has said: ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland.’”
s: for this is what Amos has said:
‘Jeroboam will die by the sword,
and Israel will surely go into exile,
away from their homeland.’”

AMO.7.12.t: And Amaziah said to Amos, “Go away, you seer! Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there.
s: And Amaziah said to Amos, “Go away, you seer! Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there.

AMO.7.13.t: But never prophesy at Bethel again, because it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom.”
s: But never prophesy at Bethel again, because it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom.”

AMO.7.14.t: “I was not a prophet,” Amos replied, “nor was I the son of a prophet; rather, I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.
s: “I was not a prophet,” Amos replied, “nor was I the son of a prophet; rather, I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.

AMO.7.15.t: But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’
s: But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’

COL.2.1.t: For I want you to know how much I am struggling for you and for those at Laodicea, and for all who have not met me face to face,
s: For I want you to know how much I am struggling for you and for those at Laodicea, and for all who have not met me face to face,

COL.2.2.t: that they may be encouraged in heart, knit together in love, and filled with the full riches of complete understanding, so that they may know the mystery of God, namely Christ,
s: that they may be encouraged in heart, knit together in love, and filled with the full riches of complete understanding, so that they may know the mystery of God, namely Christ,

COL.2.3.t: in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
s: in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

COL.2.4.t: I say this so that no one will deceive you by smooth rhetoric.
s: I say this so that no one will deceive you by smooth rhetoric.

COL.2.5.t: For although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I delight to see your orderly condition and firm faith in Christ.
s: For although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I delight to see your orderly condition and firm faith in Christ.

COL.3.1.t: Therefore, since you have been raised with Christ, strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
s: Therefore, since you have been raised with Christ, strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.

COL.3.2.t: Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
s: Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.

COL.3.3.t: For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
s: For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.

COL.3.4.t: When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
s: When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.

COL.3.8.t: But now you must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips.
s: But now you must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips.

COL.3.9.t: Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,
s: Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,

COL.3.10.t: and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator.
s: and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator.

COL.3.11.t: Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.
s: Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.

COL.3.12.t: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
s: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.

COL.3.13.t: Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
s: Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.

COL.3.14.t: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
s: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.

COL.3.15.t: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
s: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.

COL.3.16.t: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
s: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.

COL.3.17.t: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
s: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.

COL.3.22.t: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.
s: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.

COL.3.23.t: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,
s: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,

COL.3.24.t: because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
s: because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.

COL.3.25.t: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.
s: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.

COL.4.1.t: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.
s: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.

COL.4.2.t: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful,
s: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful,

COL.4.3.t: as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
s: as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.

COL.4.4.t: Pray that I may declare it clearly, as I should.
s: Pray that I may declare it clearly, as I should.

COL.4.5.t: Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time.
s: Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time.

COL.4.6.t: Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.
s: Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.

COL.4.7.t: Tychicus will tell you all the news about me. He is a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.
s: Tychicus will tell you all the news about me. He is a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.

COL.4.8.t: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us, and that he may encourage your hearts.
s: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us, and that he may encourage your hearts.

COL.4.9.t: With him I am sending Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you about everything here.
s: With him I am sending Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you about everything here.

COL.4.10.t: My fellow prisoner Aristarchus sends you greetings, as does Mark the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him: If he comes to you, welcome him.
s: My fellow prisoner Aristarchus sends you greetings, as does Mark the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him: If he comes to you, welcome him.

COL.4.11.t: Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jews among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.
s: Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jews among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.

COL.4.12.t: Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.
s: Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.

COL.4.13.t: For I testify about him that he goes to great pains for you and for those at Laodicea and Hierapolis.
s: For I testify about him that he goes to great pains for you and for those at Laodicea and Hierapolis.

DAN.1.3.t: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility—
s: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility—

DAN.1.4.t: young men without blemish, handsome, gifted in all wisdom, knowledgeable, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace—and to teach them the language and literature of the Chaldeans.
s: young men without blemish, handsome, gifted in all wisdom, knowledgeable, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace—and to teach them the language and literature of the Chaldeans.

DAN.1.5.t: The king assigned them daily provisions of the royal food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.
s: The king assigned them daily provisions of the royal food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.

DAN.1.6.t: Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
s: Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

DAN.1.7.t: The chief official gave them new names: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
s: The chief official gave them new names: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.

DAN.1.8.t: But Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.
s: But Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.

DAN.1.9.t: Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion from the chief official,
s: Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion from the chief official,

DAN.1.10.t: but he said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. For why should he see your faces looking thinner than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king!”
s: but he said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. For why should he see your faces looking thinner than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king!”

DAN.1.11.t: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
s: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

DAN.1.12.t: “Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.
s: “Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.

DAN.1.13.t: Then compare our appearances with those of the young men who are eating the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
s: Then compare our appearances with those of the young men who are eating the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”

DAN.1.14.t: So he consented to this and tested them for ten days.
s: So he consented to this and tested them for ten days.

DAN.1.15.t: And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.
s: And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.

DAN.1.16.t: So the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.
s: So the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.

DAN.1.17.t: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding in every kind of literature and wisdom. And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.
s: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding in every kind of literature and wisdom. And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.

DAN.2.17.t: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
s: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

DAN.2.18.t: urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
s: urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

DAN.2.19.t: During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and he blessed the God of heaven
s: During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and he blessed the God of heaven

DAN.2.20.t: and declared: “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.
s: and declared:
“Blessed be the name of God forever and ever,
for wisdom and power belong to Him.

DAN.2.21.t: He changes the times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes them. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning.
s: He changes the times and seasons;
He removes kings and establishes them.
He gives wisdom to the wise
and knowledge to the discerning.

DAN.2.22.t: He reveals the deep and hidden things; He knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with Him.
s: He reveals the deep and hidden things;
He knows what lies in darkness,
and light dwells with Him.

DAN.2.23.t: To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and power. And now You have made known to me what we have requested, for You have made known to us the dream of the king.”
s: To You, O God of my fathers,
I give thanks and praise,
because You have given me
wisdom and power.
And now You have made known to me
what we have requested,
for You have made known to us
the dream of the king.”

DAN.3.13.t: Then Nebuchadnezzar, furious with rage, summoned Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. So these men were brought before the king,
s: Then Nebuchadnezzar, furious with rage, summoned Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. So these men were brought before the king,

DAN.3.14.t: and Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is it true that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden statue I have set up?
s: and Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is it true that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden statue I have set up?

DAN.3.15.t: Now, if you are ready, as soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the statue I have made. But if you refuse to worship, you will be thrown at once into the blazing fiery furnace. Then what god will be able to deliver you from my hands?”
s: Now, if you are ready, as soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the statue I have made. But if you refuse to worship, you will be thrown at once into the blazing fiery furnace. Then what god will be able to deliver you from my hands?”

DAN.3.16.t: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to the king, “O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.
s: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to the king, “O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.

DAN.3.17.t: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king.
s: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king.

DAN.3.18.t: But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”
s: But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”

DAN.6.1.t: Now it pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom,
s: Now it pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom,

DAN.6.2.t: and over them three administrators, including Daniel, to whom these satraps were accountable so that the king would not suffer loss.
s: and over them three administrators, including Daniel, to whom these satraps were accountable so that the king would not suffer loss.

DAN.6.3.t: Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps. So the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.
s: Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps. So the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

DAN.6.4.t: Thus the administrators and satraps sought a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.
s: Thus the administrators and satraps sought a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.

DAN.6.5.t: Finally these men said, “We will never find any charge against this Daniel, unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God.”
s: Finally these men said, “We will never find any charge against this Daniel, unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God.”

DAN.6.6.t: So the administrators and satraps went together to the king and said, “O King Darius, may you live forever!
s: So the administrators and satraps went together to the king and said, “O King Darius, may you live forever!

DAN.6.7.t: All the royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers, and governors have agreed that the king should establish an ordinance and enforce a decree that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.
s: All the royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers, and governors have agreed that the king should establish an ordinance and enforce a decree that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.

DAN.6.8.t: Therefore, O king, establish the decree and sign the document so that it cannot be changed—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed.”
s: Therefore, O king, establish the decree and sign the document so that it cannot be changed—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed.”

DAN.6.9.t: Therefore King Darius signed the written decree.
s: Therefore King Darius signed the written decree.

DAN.6.10.t: Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house, where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks to his God, just as he had done before.
s: Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house, where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks to his God, just as he had done before.

DEU.1.26.t: But you were unwilling to go up; you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
s: But you were unwilling to go up; you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.

DEU.1.27.t: You grumbled in your tents and said, “Because the LORD hates us, He has brought us out of the land of Egypt to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to be annihilated.
s: You grumbled in your tents and said, “Because the LORD hates us, He has brought us out of the land of Egypt to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to be annihilated.

DEU.1.28.t: Where can we go? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying: ‘The people are larger and taller than we are; the cities are large, with walls up to the heavens. We even saw the descendants of the Anakim there.’”
s: Where can we go? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying: ‘The people are larger and taller than we are; the cities are large, with walls up to the heavens. We even saw the descendants of the Anakim there.’”

DEU.1.29.t: So I said to you: “Do not be terrified or afraid of them!
s: So I said to you: “Do not be terrified or afraid of them!

DEU.1.30.t: The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you, just as you saw Him do for you in Egypt
s: The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you, just as you saw Him do for you in Egypt

DEU.1.31.t: and in the wilderness, where the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way by which you traveled until you reached this place.”
s: and in the wilderness, where the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way by which you traveled until you reached this place.”

DEU.1.32.t: But in spite of all this, you did not trust the LORD your God,
s: But in spite of all this, you did not trust the LORD your God,

DEU.1.33.t: who went before you on the journey, in the fire by night and in the cloud by day, to seek out a place for you to camp and to show you the road to travel.
s: who went before you on the journey, in the fire by night and in the cloud by day, to seek out a place for you to camp and to show you the road to travel.

DEU.6.4.t: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.
s: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.

DEU.6.5.t: And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
s: And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.

DEU.6.6.t: These words I am commanding you today are to be upon your hearts.
s: These words I am commanding you today are to be upon your hearts.

DEU.6.7.t: And you shall teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
s: And you shall teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.

DEU.6.8.t: Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.
s: Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.

DEU.6.9.t: Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.
s: Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.

DEU.7.6.t: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all peoples on the face of the earth.
s: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all peoples on the face of the earth.

DEU.7.7.t: The LORD did not set His affection on you and choose you because you were more numerous than the other peoples, for you were the fewest of all peoples.
s: The LORD did not set His affection on you and choose you because you were more numerous than the other peoples, for you were the fewest of all peoples.

DEU.7.8.t: But because the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers, He brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
s: But because the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers, He brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

DEU.7.9.t: Know therefore that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations of those who love Him and keep His commandments.
s: Know therefore that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations of those who love Him and keep His commandments.

DEU.8.6.t: Therefore you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and fearing Him.
s: Therefore you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and fearing Him.

DEU.8.7.t: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of brooks and fountains and springs that flow through the valleys and hills;
s: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of brooks and fountains and springs that flow through the valleys and hills;

DEU.8.8.t: a land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of olive oil and honey;
s: a land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of olive oil and honey;

DEU.8.9.t: a land where you will eat food without scarcity, where you will lack nothing; a land whose rocks are iron and whose hills are ready to be mined for copper.
s: a land where you will eat food without scarcity, where you will lack nothing; a land whose rocks are iron and whose hills are ready to be mined for copper.

DEU.8.10.t: When you eat and are satisfied, you are to bless the LORD your God for the good land that He has given you.
s: When you eat and are satisfied, you are to bless the LORD your God for the good land that He has given you.

DEU.8.11.t: Be careful not to forget the LORD your God by failing to keep His commandments and ordinances and statutes, which I am giving you this day.
s: Be careful not to forget the LORD your God by failing to keep His commandments and ordinances and statutes, which I am giving you this day.

DEU.30.11.t: For this commandment I give you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach.
s: For this commandment I give you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach.

DEU.30.12.t: It is not in heaven, that you should need to ask, ‘Who will ascend into heaven to get it for us and proclaim it, that we may obey it?’
s: It is not in heaven, that you should need to ask, ‘Who will ascend into heaven to get it for us and proclaim it, that we may obey it?’

DEU.30.13.t: And it is not beyond the sea, that you should need to ask, ‘Who will cross the sea to get it for us and proclaim it, that we may obey it?’
s: And it is not beyond the sea, that you should need to ask, ‘Who will cross the sea to get it for us and proclaim it, that we may obey it?’

DEU.30.14.t: But the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it.
s: But the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it.

DEU.31.1.t: When Moses had finished speaking these words to all Israel,
s: When Moses had finished speaking these words to all Israel,

DEU.31.2.t: he said to them, “I am now a hundred and twenty years old; I am no longer able to come and go, and the LORD has said to me, ‘You shall not cross the Jordan.’
s: he said to them, “I am now a hundred and twenty years old; I am no longer able to come and go, and the LORD has said to me, ‘You shall not cross the Jordan.’

DEU.31.3.t: The LORD your God Himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua will cross ahead of you, as the LORD has said.
s: The LORD your God Himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua will cross ahead of you, as the LORD has said.

DEU.31.4.t: And the LORD will do to them as He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, when He destroyed them along with their land.
s: And the LORD will do to them as He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, when He destroyed them along with their land.

DEU.31.5.t: The LORD will deliver them over to you, and you must do to them exactly as I have commanded you.
s: The LORD will deliver them over to you, and you must do to them exactly as I have commanded you.

DEU.31.6.t: Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or terrified of them, for it is the LORD your God who goes with you; He will never leave you nor forsake you.”
s: Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or terrified of them, for it is the LORD your God who goes with you; He will never leave you nor forsake you.”

DEU.31.7.t: Then Moses called for Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their fathers to give them, and you shall give it to them as an inheritance.
s: Then Moses called for Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their fathers to give them, and you shall give it to them as an inheritance.

DEU.31.8.t: The LORD Himself goes before you; He will be with you. He will never leave you nor forsake you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.”
s: The LORD Himself goes before you; He will be with you. He will never leave you nor forsake you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.”

DEU.31.9.t: So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
s: So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.

DEU.31.10.t: Then Moses commanded them, “At the end of every seven years, at the appointed time in the year of remission of debt, during the Feast of Tabernacles,
s: Then Moses commanded them, “At the end of every seven years, at the appointed time in the year of remission of debt, during the Feast of Tabernacles,

DEU.31.11.t: when all Israel comes before the LORD your God at the place He will choose, you are to read this law in the hearing of all Israel.
s: when all Israel comes before the LORD your God at the place He will choose, you are to read this law in the hearing of all Israel.

DEU.31.12.t: Assemble the people—men, women, children, and the foreigners within your gates—so that they may listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and to follow carefully all the words of this law.
s: Assemble the people—men, women, children, and the foreigners within your gates—so that they may listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and to follow carefully all the words of this law.

DEU.31.13.t: Then their children who do not know the law will listen and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as you live in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
s: Then their children who do not know the law will listen and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as you live in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

DEU.33.1.t: This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced upon the Israelites before his death.
s: This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced upon the Israelites before his death.

DEU.33.2.t: He said: “The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon us from Seir; He shone forth from Mount Paran and came with myriads of holy ones, with flaming fire at His right hand.
s: He said:
“The LORD came from Sinai
and dawned upon us from Seir;
He shone forth from Mount Paran
and came with myriads of holy ones,
with flaming fire at His right hand.

DEU.33.3.t: Surely You love the people; all the holy ones are in Your hand, and they sit down at Your feet; each receives Your words—
s: Surely You love the people;
all the holy ones are in Your hand,
and they sit down at Your feet;
each receives Your words—

DEU.33.4.t: the law that Moses gave us, the possession of the assembly of Jacob.
s: the law that Moses gave us,
the possession of the assembly of Jacob.

DEU.33.5.t: So the LORD became King in Jeshurun when the leaders of the people gathered, when the tribes of Israel came together.
s: So the LORD became King in Jeshurun
when the leaders of the people gathered,
when the tribes of Israel came together.

DEU.33.6.t: Let Reuben live and not die, nor his men be few.”
s: Let Reuben live and not die,
nor his men be few.”

DEU.33.7.t: And concerning Judah he said: “O LORD, hear the cry of Judah and bring him to his people. With his own hands he defends his cause, but may You be a help against his foes.”
s: And concerning Judah he said:
“O LORD, hear the cry of Judah
and bring him to his people.
With his own hands he defends his cause,
but may You be a help against his foes.”

DEU.33.8.t: Concerning Levi he said: “Give Your Thummim to Levi and Your Urim to Your godly one, whom You tested at Massah and contested at the waters of Meribah.
s: Concerning Levi he said:
“Give Your Thummim to Levi
and Your Urim to Your godly one,
whom You tested at Massah
and contested at the waters of Meribah.

DEU.33.9.t: He said of his father and mother, ‘I do not consider them.’ He disregarded his brothers and did not know his own sons, for he kept Your word and maintained Your covenant.
s: He said of his father and mother,
‘I do not consider them.’
He disregarded his brothers
and did not know his own sons,
for he kept Your word
and maintained Your covenant.

DEU.33.10.t: He will teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel; he will set incense before You and whole burnt offerings on Your altar.
s: He will teach Your ordinances to Jacob
and Your law to Israel;
he will set incense before You
and whole burnt offerings on Your altar.

DEU.33.11.t: Bless his substance, O LORD, and accept the work of his hands. Smash the loins of those who rise against him, and of his foes so they can rise no more.”
s: Bless his substance, O LORD,
and accept the work of his hands.
Smash the loins of those who rise against him,
and of his foes so they can rise no more.”

DEU.33.12.t: Concerning Benjamin he said: “May the beloved of the LORD rest secure in Him; God shields him all day long, and upon His shoulders he rests.”
s: Concerning Benjamin he said:
“May the beloved of the LORD
rest secure in Him;
God shields him all day long,
and upon His shoulders he rests.”

DEU.33.26.t: “There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your aid, and the clouds in His majesty.
s: “There is none like the God of Jeshurun,
who rides the heavens to your aid,
and the clouds in His majesty.

DEU.33.27.t: The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He drives out the enemy before you, giving the command, ‘Destroy him!’
s: The eternal God is your dwelling place,
and underneath are the everlasting arms.
He drives out the enemy before you,
giving the command, ‘Destroy him!’

DEU.33.28.t: So Israel dwells securely; the fountain of Jacob lives untroubled in a land of grain and new wine, where even the heavens drip with dew.
s: So Israel dwells securely;
the fountain of Jacob lives untroubled
in a land of grain and new wine,
where even the heavens drip with dew.

DEU.33.29.t: Blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is the shield that protects you, the sword in which you boast. Your enemies will cower before you, and you shall trample their high places.”
s: Blessed are you, O Israel!
Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD?
He is the shield that protects you,
the sword in which you boast.
Your enemies will cower before you,
and you shall trample their high places.”

ECC.3.1.t: To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
s: To everything there is a season,
and a time for every purpose under heaven:

ECC.3.2.t: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,
s: a time to be born and a time to die,
a time to plant and a time to uproot,

ECC.3.3.t: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build,
s: a time to kill and a time to heal,
a time to break down and a time to build,

ECC.3.4.t: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,
s: a time to weep and a time to laugh,
a time to mourn and a time to dance,

ECC.3.5.t: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,
s: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together,
a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,

ECC.3.6.t: a time to search and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to discard,
s: a time to search and a time to count as lost,
a time to keep and a time to discard,

ECC.3.7.t: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
s: a time to tear and a time to mend,
a time to be silent and a time to speak,

ECC.3.8.t: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
s: a time to love and a time to hate,
a time for war and a time for peace.

ECC.3.9.t: What does the worker gain from his toil?
s: What does the worker gain from his toil?

ECC.3.10.t: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.
s: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.

ECC.3.11.t: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.
s: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.

ECC.3.12.t: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,
s: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,

ECC.3.13.t: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
s: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.

ECC.3.14.t: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.
s: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.

ECC.4.7.t: Again, I saw futility under the sun.
s: Again, I saw futility under the sun.

ECC.4.8.t: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
s: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.

ECC.4.9.t: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.
s: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.

ECC.4.10.t: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
s: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!

ECC.4.11.t: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
s: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?

ECC.4.12.t: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
s: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

ECC.9.7.t: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:
s: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:

ECC.9.8.t: Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.
s: Let your garments always be white,
and never spare the oil for your head.

ECC.9.9.t: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
s: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.

ECC.9.10.t: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
s: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

ECC.9.11.t: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.
s: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.

ECC.9.12.t: For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.
s: For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.

ECC.9.13.t: I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:
s: I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:

ECC.9.14.t: There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.
s: There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.

ECC.9.15.t: Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
s: Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.

ECC.9.16.t: And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”
s: And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”

ECC.9.17.t: The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.
s: The calm words of the wise are heeded
over the shouts of a ruler among fools.

ECC.9.18.t: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
s: Wisdom is better than weapons of war,
but one sinner destroys much good.

ECC.11.1.t: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
s: Cast your bread upon the waters,
for after many days you will find it again.

ECC.11.2.t: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.
s: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight,
for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.

ECC.11.3.t: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
s: If the clouds are full,
they will pour out rain upon the earth;
whether a tree falls to the south or to the north,
in the place where it falls, there it will lie.

ECC.11.4.t: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.
s: He who watches the wind will fail to sow,
and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.

ECC.11.5.t: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
s: As you do not know the path of the wind,
or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb,
so you cannot understand the work of God,
the Maker of all things.

ECC.11.6.t: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
s: Sow your seed in the morning,
and do not rest your hands in the evening,
for you do not know which will succeed,
whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.

EPH.1.3.t: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.
s: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.

EPH.1.4.t: For He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless in His presence. In love
s: For He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless in His presence. In love

EPH.1.5.t: He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,
s: He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,

EPH.1.6.t: to the praise of His glorious grace, which He has freely given us in the Beloved One.
s: to the praise of His glorious grace, which He has freely given us in the Beloved One.

EPH.2.4.t: But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy,
s: But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy,

EPH.2.5.t: made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses. It is by grace you have been saved!
s: made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses. It is by grace you have been saved!

EPH.2.6.t: And God raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus,
s: And God raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus,

EPH.2.7.t: in order that in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace, demonstrated by His kindness to us in Christ Jesus.
s: in order that in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace, demonstrated by His kindness to us in Christ Jesus.

EPH.2.8.t: For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,
s: For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,

EPH.2.9.t: not by works, so that no one can boast.
s: not by works, so that no one can boast.

EPH.2.10.t: For we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life.
s: For we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life.

EPH.3.14.t: ... for this reason I bow my knees before the Father,
s: ... for this reason I bow my knees before the Father,

EPH.3.15.t: from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name.
s: from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name.

EPH.3.16.t: I ask that out of the riches of His glory He may strengthen you with power through His Spirit in your inner being,
s: I ask that out of the riches of His glory He may strengthen you with power through His Spirit in your inner being,

EPH.3.17.t: so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith. Then you, being rooted and grounded in love,
s: so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith. Then you, being rooted and grounded in love,

EPH.3.18.t: will have power, together with all the saints, to comprehend the length and width and height and depth
s: will have power, together with all the saints, to comprehend the length and width and height and depth

EPH.3.19.t: of the love of Christ, and to know this love that surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
s: of the love of Christ, and to know this love that surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.

EPH.3.20.t: Now to Him who is able to do so much more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us,
s: Now to Him who is able to do so much more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us,

EPH.3.21.t: to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
s: to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

EPH.4.1.t: As a prisoner in the Lord, then, I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received:
s: As a prisoner in the Lord, then, I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received:

EPH.4.2.t: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
s: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,

EPH.4.3.t: and with diligence to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.
s: and with diligence to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.

EPH.4.4.t: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called;
s: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called;

EPH.4.5.t: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
s: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;

EPH.4.6.t: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
s: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

EPH.4.20.t: But this is not the way you came to know Christ.
s: But this is not the way you came to know Christ.

EPH.4.21.t: Surely you heard of Him and were taught in Him—in keeping with the truth that is in Jesus—
s: Surely you heard of Him and were taught in Him—in keeping with the truth that is in Jesus—

EPH.4.22.t: to put off your former way of life, your old self, which is being corrupted by its deceitful desires;
s: to put off your former way of life, your old self, which is being corrupted by its deceitful desires;

EPH.4.23.t: to be renewed in the spirit of your minds;
s: to be renewed in the spirit of your minds;

EPH.4.24.t: and to put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.
s: and to put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.

EPH.4.25.t: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor, for we are all members of one another.
s: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor, for we are all members of one another.

EPH.4.26.t: “Be angry, yet do not sin.” Do not let the sun set upon your anger,
s: “Be angry, yet do not sin.” Do not let the sun set upon your anger,

EPH.4.27.t: and do not give the devil a foothold.
s: and do not give the devil a foothold.

EPH.4.28.t: He who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing good with his own hands, that he may have something to share with the one in need.
s: He who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing good with his own hands, that he may have something to share with the one in need.

EPH.4.29.t: Let no unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen.
s: Let no unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen.

EPH.4.30.t: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
s: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

EPH.4.31.t: Get rid of all bitterness, rage and anger, outcry and slander, along with every form of malice.
s: Get rid of all bitterness, rage and anger, outcry and slander, along with every form of malice.

EPH.4.32.t: Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.
s: Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.

EPH.5.1.t: Be imitators of God, therefore, as beloved children,
s: Be imitators of God, therefore, as beloved children,

EPH.5.2.t: and walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God.
s: and walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God.

EST.2.5.t: Now there was at the citadel of Susa a Jewish man from the tribe of Benjamin named Mordecai son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish.
s: Now there was at the citadel of Susa a Jewish man from the tribe of Benjamin named Mordecai son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish.

EST.2.6.t: He had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon among those taken captive with Jeconiah king of Judah.
s: He had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon among those taken captive with Jeconiah king of Judah.

EST.2.7.t: And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther), the daughter of his uncle, because she did not have a father or mother. The young woman was lovely in form and appearance, and when her father and mother had died, Mordecai had taken her in as his own daughter.
s: And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther), the daughter of his uncle, because she did not have a father or mother. The young woman was lovely in form and appearance, and when her father and mother had died, Mordecai had taken her in as his own daughter.

EST.2.8.t: When the king’s command and edict had been proclaimed, many young women gathered at the citadel of Susa under the care of Hegai. Esther was also taken to the palace and placed under the care of Hegai, the custodian of the women.
s: When the king’s command and edict had been proclaimed, many young women gathered at the citadel of Susa under the care of Hegai. Esther was also taken to the palace and placed under the care of Hegai, the custodian of the women.

EST.2.9.t: And the young woman pleased him and obtained his favor, so he quickly provided her with beauty treatments and the special diet. He assigned to her seven select maidservants from the palace and transferred her with them to the best place in the harem.
s: And the young woman pleased him and obtained his favor, so he quickly provided her with beauty treatments and the special diet. He assigned to her seven select maidservants from the palace and transferred her with them to the best place in the harem.

EST.2.10.t: Esther did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.
s: Esther did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.

EST.2.11.t: And every day Mordecai would walk back and forth in front of the court of the harem to learn about Esther’s welfare and what was happening to her.
s: And every day Mordecai would walk back and forth in front of the court of the harem to learn about Esther’s welfare and what was happening to her.

EXO.1.15.t: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,
s: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,

EXO.1.16.t: “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”
s: “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”

EXO.1.17.t: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.
s: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.

EXO.1.18.t: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”
s: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”

EXO.1.19.t: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”
s: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”

EXO.1.20.t: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.
s: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.

EXO.1.21.t: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.
s: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.

EXO.2.1.t: Now a man of the house of Levi married a daughter of Levi,
s: Now a man of the house of Levi married a daughter of Levi,

EXO.2.2.t: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.
s: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.

EXO.2.3.t: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
s: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.

EXO.2.4.t: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
s: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

EXO.2.5.t: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. And when she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maidservant to retrieve it.
s: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. And when she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maidservant to retrieve it.

EXO.2.6.t: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
s: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”

EXO.2.7.t: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”
s: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”

EXO.2.8.t: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.
s: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.

EXO.2.9.t: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.
s: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.

EXO.2.10.t: When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”
s: When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”

EXO.2.15.t: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down beside a well.
s: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down beside a well.

EXO.2.16.t: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.
s: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.

EXO.2.17.t: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away, Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock.
s: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away, Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock.

EXO.2.18.t: When the daughters returned to their father Reuel, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”
s: When the daughters returned to their father Reuel, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”

EXO.2.19.t: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they replied. “He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”
s: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they replied. “He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”

EXO.2.20.t: “So where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.”
s: “So where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.”

EXO.2.21.t: Moses agreed to stay with the man, and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.
s: Moses agreed to stay with the man, and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.

EXO.3.1.t: Meanwhile, Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
s: Meanwhile, Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

EXO.3.2.t: There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush. Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.
s: There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush. Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.

EXO.3.3.t: So Moses thought, “I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?”
s: So Moses thought, “I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?”

EXO.3.4.t: When the LORD saw that he had gone over to look, God called out to him from within the bush, “Moses, Moses!” “Here I am,” he answered.
s: When the LORD saw that he had gone over to look, God called out to him from within the bush, “Moses, Moses!”
“Here I am,” he answered.

EXO.3.5.t: “Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”
s: “Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”

EXO.3.6.t: Then He said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
s: Then He said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.”
At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.

EXO.3.7.t: The LORD said, “I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.
s: The LORD said, “I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.

EXO.3.8.t: I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
s: I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

EXO.3.9.t: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached Me, and I have seen how severely the Egyptians are oppressing them.
s: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached Me, and I have seen how severely the Egyptians are oppressing them.

EXO.3.10.t: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”
s: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”

EXO.4.10.t: “Please, Lord,” Moses replied, “I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.”
s: “Please, Lord,” Moses replied, “I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.”

EXO.4.11.t: And the LORD said to him, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
s: And the LORD said to him, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?

EXO.4.12.t: Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.”
s: Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.”

EXO.4.13.t: But Moses replied, “Please, Lord, send someone else.”
s: But Moses replied, “Please, Lord, send someone else.”

EXO.4.14.t: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
s: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.

EXO.4.15.t: You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will help both of you to speak, and I will teach you what to do.
s: You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will help both of you to speak, and I will teach you what to do.

EXO.4.16.t: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and it will be as if you were God to him.
s: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and it will be as if you were God to him.

EXO.4.17.t: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.”
s: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.”

EXO.17.8.t: After this, the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
s: After this, the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.

EXO.17.9.t: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.”
s: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.”

EXO.17.10.t: Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
s: Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

EXO.17.11.t: As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed; but when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.
s: As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed; but when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.

EXO.17.12.t: When Moses’ hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
s: When Moses’ hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.

EXO.17.13.t: So Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his army with the sword.
s: So Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his army with the sword.

EXO.18.13.t: The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
s: The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.

EXO.18.14.t: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?”
s: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?”

EXO.18.15.t: “Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.
s: “Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.

EXO.18.16.t: “Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me to judge between one man and another, and I make known to them the statutes and laws of God.”
s: “Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me to judge between one man and another, and I make known to them the statutes and laws of God.”

EXO.18.17.t: But Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing is not good.
s: But Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing is not good.
