LUK.2.25.t: Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
s: Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.

LUK.2.26.t: The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
s: The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.

LUK.2.27.t: Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple courts. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for Him what was customary under the Law,
s: Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple courts. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for Him what was customary under the Law,

LUK.2.28.t: Simeon took Him in his arms and blessed God, saying:
s: Simeon took Him in his arms and blessed God, saying:

LUK.2.29.t: “Sovereign Lord, as You have promised, You now dismiss Your servant in peace.
s: “Sovereign Lord, as You have promised,
You now dismiss Your servant in peace.

LUK.2.30.t: For my eyes have seen Your salvation,
s: For my eyes have seen Your salvation,

LUK.2.31.t: which You have prepared in the sight of all people,
s: which You have prepared in the sight of all people,

LUK.2.32.t: a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to Your people Israel.”
s: a light for revelation to the Gentiles,
and for glory to Your people Israel.”

LUK.2.33.t: The Child’s father and mother were amazed at what was spoken about Him.
s: The Child’s father and mother were amazed at what was spoken about Him.

LUK.2.34.t: Then Simeon blessed them and said to His mother Mary: “Behold, this Child is appointed to cause the rise and fall of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be spoken against,
s: Then Simeon blessed them and said to His mother Mary:
“Behold, this Child is appointed to cause
the rise and fall of many in Israel,
and to be a sign that will be spoken against,

LUK.2.35.t: so that the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed— and a sword will pierce your soul as well.”
s: so that the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed—
and a sword will pierce your soul as well.”

LUK.2.36.t: There was also a prophetess named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, who was well along in years. She had been married for seven years,
s: There was also a prophetess named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, who was well along in years. She had been married for seven years,

LUK.2.37.t: and then was a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple, but worshiped night and day, fasting and praying.
s: and then was a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple, but worshiped night and day, fasting and praying.

LUK.2.38.t: Coming forward at that moment, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
s: Coming forward at that moment, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.

LUK.2.39.t: When Jesus’ parents had done everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
s: When Jesus’ parents had done everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.

s: Every year His parents went to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover.

LUK.2.43.t: When those days were over and they were returning home, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware He had stayed.
s: When those days were over and they were returning home, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware He had stayed.

s: Assuming He was in their company, they traveled on for a day before they began to look for Him among their relatives and friends.

s: When they could not find Him, they returned to Jerusalem to search for Him.

s: Finally, after three days they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.

s: And all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers.

s: “Why were you looking for Me?” He asked. “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house ?”

s: But they did not understand the statement He was making to them.

s: Then He went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. But His mother treasured up all these things in her heart.

s: And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.

s: The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”

s: Even tax collectors came to be baptized. “Teacher,” they asked, “what should we do?”

s: Then some soldiers asked him, “And what should we do?”
“Do not take money by force or false accusation,” he said. “Be content with your wages.”

s: After Jesus had left the synagogue, He went to the home of Simon, whose mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever. So they appealed to Jesus on her behalf,

s: and He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. And she got up at once and began to serve them.

s: At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Jesus, and laying His hands on each one, He healed them.

s: Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ.

s: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,

s: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.

s: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.

s: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

s: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”

s: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.

s: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.

LUK.6.27.t: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
s: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

LUK.6.28.t: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
s: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.

s: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.

s: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.

LUK.6.31.t: Do to others as you would have them do to you.
s: Do to others as you would have them do to you.

s: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.

LUK.6.33.t: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
s: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.

LUK.6.34.t: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.
s: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.

s: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.

LUK.6.36.t: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
s: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

s: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

s: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.

s: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

s: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

s: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.

s: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.

s: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”

LUK.7.14.t: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”
s: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”

LUK.7.15.t: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.
s: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.

LUK.7.16.t: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”
s: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”

s: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.

LUK.9.51.t: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.
s: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.

LUK.9.52.t: He sent messengers on ahead, who went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him.
s: He sent messengers on ahead, who went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him.

s: But the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem.

s: When the disciples James and John saw this, they asked, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?”

LUK.9.55.t: But Jesus turned and rebuked them.
s: But Jesus turned and rebuked them.

LUK.9.56.t: And He and His disciples went on to another village.
s: And He and His disciples went on to another village.

s: The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”

LUK.10.18.t: So He told them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
s: So He told them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.

LUK.10.19.t: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.
s: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.

s: Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

s: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.

s: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

s: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”

s: He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”

s: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”

s: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”

s: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.

s: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

s: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.

LUK.10.33.t: But when a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion.
s: But when a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion.

s: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

s: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’

s: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”

LUK.10.37.t: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law. Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”
s: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law.
Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”

s: As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.

s: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.

s: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”

s: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.

s: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”

s: So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say:

Your kingdom come.

s: And forgive us our sins,
for we also forgive everyone who sins against us.
And lead us not into temptation.’”

s: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.

s: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!

s: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

LUK.12.26.t: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
s: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?

s: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

s: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!

LUK.12.29.t: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.
s: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.

s: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.

LUK.12.31.t: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.
s: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.

LUK.12.32.t: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
s: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.

s: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

s: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.

s: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,

s: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’

s: In the same way, I tell you that there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.

s: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.

s: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.

s: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.

LUK.15.26.t: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
s: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.

LUK.15.27.t: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’
s: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’

LUK.15.28.t: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
s: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

LUK.15.29.t: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
s: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.

LUK.15.30.t: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
s: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’

LUK.15.31.t: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.
s: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.

LUK.15.32.t: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
s: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”

LUK.16.1.t: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
s: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.

LUK.16.2.t: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
s: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’

LUK.16.3.t: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
s: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.

LUK.16.4.t: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
s: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’

LUK.16.5.t: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
s: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.

LUK.16.6.t: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
s: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered.
‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

LUK.16.7.t: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
s: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’
‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied.
‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.

LUK.16.8.t: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
s: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

LUK.16.9.t: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
s: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

LUK.16.10.t: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
s: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.

LUK.16.11.t: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
s: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?

LUK.16.12.t: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
s: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?

LUK.16.13.t: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
s: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”

LUK.17.1.t: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
s: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!

LUK.17.2.t: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
s: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.

LUK.17.3.t: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
s: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.

LUK.17.4.t: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”
s: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

LUK.17.5.t: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
s: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”

LUK.17.6.t: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
s: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.

LUK.17.7.t: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
s: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?

LUK.17.8.t: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink; and afterward you may eat and drink’?
s: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink; and afterward you may eat and drink’?

LUK.17.9.t: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?
s: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?

LUK.17.10.t: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”
s: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”

LUK.17.11.t: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
s: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.

LUK.17.12.t: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance
s: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance

LUK.17.13.t: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
s: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

LUK.17.14.t: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
s: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.

LUK.17.15.t: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.
s: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.

LUK.17.16.t: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.
s: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.

LUK.17.17.t: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?
s: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?

LUK.17.18.t: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”
s: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”

LUK.17.19.t: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”
s: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”

LUK.18.9.t: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:
s: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:

LUK.18.10.t: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
s: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

LUK.18.11.t: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like the other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
s: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like the other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.

LUK.18.12.t: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’
s: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’

LUK.18.13.t: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’
s: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’

LUK.18.14.t: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
s: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

LUK.19.1.t: Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.
s: Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.

LUK.19.2.t: And there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.
s: And there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.

LUK.19.3.t: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature.
s: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature.

LUK.19.4.t: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him, since Jesus was about to pass that way.
s: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him, since Jesus was about to pass that way.

LUK.19.5.t: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”
s: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”

LUK.19.6.t: So Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully.
s: So Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully.

LUK.19.7.t: And all who saw this began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”
s: And all who saw this began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”

LUK.19.8.t: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”
s: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”

LUK.19.9.t: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
s: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.

LUK.19.10.t: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
s: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”

LUK.22.31.t: Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift each of you like wheat.
s: Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift each of you like wheat.

LUK.22.32.t: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
s: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”

LUK.22.33.t: “Lord,” said Peter, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.”
s: “Lord,” said Peter, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.”

LUK.22.34.t: But Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”
s: But Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”

LUK.23.32.t: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.
s: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.

LUK.23.33.t: When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.
s: When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.

LUK.23.34.t: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up His garments by casting lots.
s: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up His garments by casting lots.

LUK.23.35.t: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”
s: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”

LUK.23.36.t: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.
s: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.

LUK.23.37.t: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”
s: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”

LUK.23.38.t: Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
s: Above Him was posted an inscription:
THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

LUK.24.13.t: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
s: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.

LUK.24.14.t: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
s: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.

LUK.24.15.t: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.
s: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.

LUK.24.16.t: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.
s: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.

LUK.24.17.t: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?” They stood still, with sadness on their faces.
s: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?”
They stood still, with sadness on their faces.

LUK.24.18.t: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”
s: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”

LUK.24.19.t: “What things?” He asked. “The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.
s: “What things?” He asked.
“The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.

LUK.24.20.t: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.
s: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.

LUK.24.21.t: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.
s: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.

LUK.24.22.t: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,
s: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,

LUK.24.23.t: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.
s: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.

LUK.24.24.t: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”
s: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”

LUK.24.25.t: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, how slow are your hearts to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
s: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, how slow are your hearts to believe all that the prophets have spoken!

LUK.24.26.t: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”
s: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”

LUK.24.27.t: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.
s: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.

LUK.24.28.t: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.
s: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.

LUK.24.29.t: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.” So He went in to stay with them.
s: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.”
So He went in to stay with them.

LUK.24.30.t: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.
s: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.

LUK.24.31.t: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus—and He disappeared from their sight.
s: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus—and He disappeared from their sight.

LUK.24.32.t: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
s: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”

MAT.1.18.t: This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about: His mother Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit.
s: This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about: His mother Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit.

MAT.1.19.t: Because Joseph her husband was a righteous man and was unwilling to disgrace her publicly, he resolved to divorce her quietly.
s: Because Joseph her husband was a righteous man and was unwilling to disgrace her publicly, he resolved to divorce her quietly.

MAT.1.20.t: But after he had pondered these things, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife, for the One conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
s: But after he had pondered these things, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife, for the One conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.

MAT.1.21.t: She will give birth to a Son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.”
s: She will give birth to a Son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.”

MAT.1.22.t: All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:
s: All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:

MAT.1.23.t: “Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel” (which means, “God with us”).
s: “Behold, the virgin will be with child
and will give birth to a son,
and they will call Him Immanuel”
(which means, “God with us”).

MAT.1.24.t: When Joseph woke up, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and embraced Mary as his wife.
s: When Joseph woke up, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and embraced Mary as his wife.

MAT.1.25.t: But he had no union with her until she gave birth to a Son. And he gave Him the name Jesus.
s: But he had no union with her until she gave birth to a Son. And he gave Him the name Jesus.

MAT.4.1.t: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
s: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

MAT.4.2.t: After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry.
s: After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry.

MAT.4.3.t: The tempter came to Him and said, “If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”
s: The tempter came to Him and said, “If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”

MAT.4.4.t: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
s: But Jesus answered, “It is written:
‘Man shall not live on bread alone,
but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”

MAT.4.5.t: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.
s: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.

MAT.4.6.t: “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down. For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You, and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’”
s: “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down. For it is written:
‘He will command His angels concerning You,
and they will lift You up in their hands,
so that You will not strike Your foot
against a stone.’”

MAT.4.7.t: Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
s: Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

MAT.4.8.t: Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
s: Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.

MAT.4.9.t: “All this I will give You,” he said, “if You will fall down and worship me.”
s: “All this I will give You,” he said, “if You will fall down and worship me.”

MAT.4.10.t: “Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus declared. “For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’”
s: “Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus declared. “For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’”

MAT.4.11.t: Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.
s: Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.

MAT.4.18.t: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
s: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

MAT.4.19.t: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
s: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”

MAT.4.20.t: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
s: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.

MAT.4.21.t: Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them,
s: Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them,

MAT.4.22.t: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.
s: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.

MAT.5.1.t: When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to Him,
s: When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to Him,

MAT.5.2.t: and He began to teach them, saying:
s: and He began to teach them, saying:

MAT.5.3.t: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
s: “Blessed are the poor in spirit,
for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

MAT.5.4.t: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
s: Blessed are those who mourn,
for they will be comforted.

MAT.5.5.t: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
s: Blessed are the meek,
for they will inherit the earth.

MAT.5.6.t: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
s: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,
for they will be filled.

MAT.5.7.t: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
s: Blessed are the merciful,
for they will be shown mercy.

MAT.5.8.t: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
s: Blessed are the pure in heart,
for they will see God.

MAT.5.9.t: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
s: Blessed are the peacemakers,
for they will be called sons of God.

MAT.5.10.t: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
s: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness,
for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

MAT.5.11.t: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.
s: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.

MAT.5.12.t: Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven; for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you.
s: Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven; for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you.

MAT.5.13.t: You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men.
s: You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men.

MAT.5.14.t: You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
s: You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.

MAT.5.15.t: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
s: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.

MAT.5.16.t: In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.
s: In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.

MAT.5.21.t: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not murder’ and ‘Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’
s: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not murder’ and ‘Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’

MAT.5.22.t: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of hell.
s: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of hell.

MAT.5.23.t: So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
s: So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,

MAT.5.24.t: leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.
s: leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.

MAT.5.25.t: Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court. Otherwise, he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.
s: Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court. Otherwise, he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.

MAT.5.26.t: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.
s: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.

MAT.5.33.t: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
s: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’

MAT.5.34.t: But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;
s: But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;

MAT.5.35.t: or by the earth, for it is His footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
s: or by the earth, for it is His footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

MAT.5.36.t: Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.
s: Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.

MAT.5.37.t: Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one.
s: Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one.

MAT.6.1.t: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
s: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.

MAT.6.2.t: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
s: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

MAT.6.3.t: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
s: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

MAT.6.4.t: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
s: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

MAT.6.5.t: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
s: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

MAT.6.6.t: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
s: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

MAT.6.7.t: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.
s: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.

MAT.6.8.t: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
s: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

MAT.6.9.t: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.
s: So then, this is how you should pray:
‘Our Father in heaven,
hallowed be Your name.

MAT.6.10.t: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
s: Your kingdom come,
Your will be done,
on earth as it is in heaven.

MAT.6.11.t: Give us this day our daily bread.
s: Give us this day our daily bread.

MAT.6.12.t: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
s: And forgive us our debts,
as we also have forgiven our debtors.

MAT.6.13.t: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’
s: And lead us not into temptation,
but deliver us from the evil one.’

MAT.6.14.t: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
s: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

MAT.6.15.t: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.
s: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.

MAT.6.25.t: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
s: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

MAT.6.26.t: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns—and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?
s: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns—and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

MAT.6.27.t: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
s: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

MAT.6.28.t: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.
s: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.

MAT.6.29.t: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
s: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

MAT.6.30.t: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
s: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

MAT.6.31.t: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
s: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

MAT.6.32.t: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
s: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

MAT.6.33.t: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.
s: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.

MAT.6.34.t: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.
s: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.

MAT.7.7.t: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
s: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

MAT.7.8.t: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
s: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

MAT.7.9.t: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
s: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

MAT.7.10.t: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
s: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?

MAT.7.11.t: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!
s: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!

MAT.7.15.t: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
s: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.

MAT.7.16.t: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
s: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

MAT.7.17.t: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
s: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.

MAT.7.18.t: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
s: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.

MAT.7.19.t: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
s: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

MAT.7.20.t: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.
s: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.

MAT.7.24.t: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
s: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

MAT.7.25.t: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.
s: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.

MAT.7.26.t: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
s: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

MAT.7.27.t: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and great was its collapse!”
s: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and great was its collapse!”

MAT.9.35.t: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.
s: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.

MAT.9.36.t: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
s: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.

MAT.9.37.t: Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
s: Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.

MAT.9.38.t: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”
s: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”

MAT.10.26.t: So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
s: So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

MAT.10.27.t: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.
s: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.

MAT.10.28.t: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
s: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.

MAT.10.29.t: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.
s: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.

MAT.10.30.t: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
s: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

MAT.10.31.t: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
s: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

MAT.11.25.t: At that time Jesus declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.
s: At that time Jesus declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.

MAT.11.26.t: Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
s: Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.

MAT.11.27.t: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
s: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.

MAT.11.28.t: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
s: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

MAT.11.29.t: Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
s: Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.

MAT.11.30.t: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”
s: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”

MAT.14.22.t: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.
s: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.

MAT.14.23.t: After He had sent them away, He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. When evening came, He was there alone,
s: After He had sent them away, He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. When evening came, He was there alone,

MAT.14.24.t: but the boat was already far from land, buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.
s: but the boat was already far from land, buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.

MAT.14.25.t: During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.
s: During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.

MAT.14.26.t: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost!” they said, and cried out in fear.
s: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost!” they said, and cried out in fear.

MAT.14.27.t: But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
s: But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”

MAT.14.28.t: “Lord, if it is You,” Peter replied, “command me to come to You on the water.”
s: “Lord, if it is You,” Peter replied, “command me to come to You on the water.”

MAT.14.29.t: “Come,” said Jesus. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.
s: “Come,” said Jesus.
Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.

MAT.14.30.t: But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”
s: But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”

MAT.14.31.t: Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”
s: Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”

MAT.14.32.t: And when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.
s: And when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.

MAT.14.33.t: Then those who were in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly You are the Son of God!”
s: Then those who were in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly You are the Son of God!”

MAT.18.1.t: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
s: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”

MAT.18.2.t: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.
s: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.

MAT.18.3.t: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
s: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

MAT.18.4.t: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
s: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

MAT.18.5.t: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.
s: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.

MAT.18.6.t: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
s: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.

MAT.18.7.t: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!
s: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!

MAT.18.8.t: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
s: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.

MAT.18.9.t: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
s: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.

MAT.18.10.t: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.
s: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.

MAT.18.12.t: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
s: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?

MAT.18.13.t: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
s: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.

MAT.18.14.t: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.
s: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.

MAT.18.15.t: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.
s: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.

MAT.18.16.t: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
s: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’

MAT.18.17.t: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.
s: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.

MAT.18.18.t: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
s: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

MAT.18.19.t: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.
s: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.

MAT.18.20.t: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”
s: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”

MAT.18.21.t: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
s: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”

MAT.18.22.t: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
s: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!

MAT.21.12.t: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
s: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.

MAT.21.13.t: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’”
s: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’”

MAT.21.14.t: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them.
s: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them.

MAT.21.15.t: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”
s: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”

MAT.21.16.t: “Do you hear what these children are saying?” they asked. “Yes,” Jesus answered. “Have you never read: ‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise’?”
s: “Do you hear what these children are saying?” they asked.
“Yes,” Jesus answered. “Have you never read:
‘From the mouths of children and infants
You have ordained praise’?”

MAT.22.34.t: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.
s: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.

MAT.22.35.t: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:
s: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:

MAT.22.36.t: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”
s: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”

MAT.22.37.t: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’
s: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’

MAT.22.38.t: This is the first and greatest commandment.
s: This is the first and greatest commandment.

MAT.22.39.t: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
s: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’

MAT.22.40.t: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”
s: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”

MAT.25.14.t: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.
s: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.

MAT.25.15.t: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent—each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.
s: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent—each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.

MAT.25.16.t: The servant who had received the five talents went at once and put them to work and gained five more.
s: The servant who had received the five talents went at once and put them to work and gained five more.

MAT.25.17.t: Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.
s: Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.

MAT.25.18.t: But the servant who had received the one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.
s: But the servant who had received the one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

MAT.25.19.t: After a long time the master of those servants returned to settle accounts with them.
s: After a long time the master of those servants returned to settle accounts with them.

MAT.25.20.t: The servant who had received the five talents came and presented five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.’
s: The servant who had received the five talents came and presented five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.’

MAT.25.21.t: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
s: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

MAT.25.22.t: The servant who had received the two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. See, I have gained two more.’
s: The servant who had received the two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. See, I have gained two more.’

MAT.25.23.t: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
s: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

MAT.25.24.t: Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.
s: Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.

MAT.25.25.t: So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’
s: So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’

MAT.25.26.t: ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed.
s: ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed.

MAT.25.27.t: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.
s: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.

MAT.25.28.t: Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.
s: Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.

MAT.25.29.t: For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
s: For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

MAT.25.30.t: And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
s: And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

MAT.26.36.t: At that time Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and He told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
s: At that time Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and He told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

MAT.26.37.t: He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee and began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.
s: He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee and began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.

MAT.26.38.t: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”
s: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”

MAT.26.39.t: Going a little farther, He fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Yet not as I will, but as You will.”
s: Going a little farther, He fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Yet not as I will, but as You will.”

MAT.26.40.t: Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?” He asked Peter.
s: Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?” He asked Peter.

MAT.26.41.t: “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
s: “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”

MAT.26.42.t: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”
s: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”

MAT.26.43.t: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping—for their eyes were heavy.
s: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping—for their eyes were heavy.

MAT.26.44.t: So He left them and went away once more and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.
s: So He left them and went away once more and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.

MAT.26.45.t: Then He returned to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
s: Then He returned to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

MAT.26.46.t: Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!”
s: Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!”

MAT.28.16.t: Meanwhile, the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had designated.
s: Meanwhile, the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had designated.

MAT.28.17.t: When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, but some doubted.
s: When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, but some doubted.

MAT.28.18.t: Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.
s: Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.

MAT.28.19.t: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,
s: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,

MAT.28.20.t: and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
s: and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”

MIC.6.1.t: Hear now what the LORD says: “Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
s: Hear now what the LORD says:
“Arise, plead your case before the mountains,
