and let the hills hear your voice.

MIC.6.2.t: Hear, O mountains, the LORD’s indictment, you enduring foundations of the earth. For the LORD has a case against His people, and He will argue it against Israel:
s: Hear, O mountains, the LORD’s indictment,
you enduring foundations of the earth.
For the LORD has a case against His people,
and He will argue it against Israel:

MIC.6.3.t: ‘My people, what have I done to you? Testify against Me how I have wearied you!
s: ‘My people, what have I done to you?
Testify against Me how I have wearied you!

MIC.6.4.t: For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses before you, as well as Aaron and Miriam.
s: For I brought you up from the land of Egypt
and redeemed you from the house of slavery.
I sent Moses before you,
as well as Aaron and Miriam.

MIC.6.5.t: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab counseled and what Balaam son of Beor answered. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may acknowledge the righteousness of the LORD.’”
s: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab counseled
and what Balaam son of Beor answered.
Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal,
so that you may acknowledge the righteousness of the LORD.’”

MIC.6.6.t: With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high? Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
s: With what shall I come before the LORD
when I bow before the God on high?
Should I come to Him with burnt offerings,
with year-old calves?

MIC.6.7.t: Would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I present my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
s: Would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams,
with ten thousand rivers of oil?
Shall I present my firstborn for my transgression,
the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?

MIC.6.8.t: He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
s: He has shown you, O man, what is good.
And what does the LORD require of you
but to act justly, to love mercy,
and to walk humbly with your God?

MIC.7.7.t: But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
s: But as for me, I will look to the LORD;
I will wait for the God of my salvation.
My God will hear me.

MIC.7.8.t: Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
s: Do not gloat over me, my enemy!
Though I have fallen, I will arise;
though I sit in darkness,
the LORD will be my light.

MIC.7.9.t: Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD, until He argues my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see His righteousness.
s: Because I have sinned against Him,
I must endure the rage of the LORD,
until He argues my case
and executes justice for me.
He will bring me into the light;
I will see His righteousness.

MIC.7.18.t: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance— who does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?
s: Who is a God like You,
who pardons iniquity
and passes over the transgression
of the remnant of His inheritance—
who does not retain His anger forever,
because He delights in loving devotion?

MIC.7.19.t: He will again have compassion on us; He will vanquish our iniquities. You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea.
s: He will again have compassion on us;
He will vanquish our iniquities.
You will cast out all our sins
into the depths of the sea.

MIC.7.20.t: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old.
s: You will show faithfulness to Jacob
and loving devotion to Abraham,
as You swore to our fathers
from the days of old.

MRK.1.40.t: Then a leper came to Jesus, begging on his knees: “If You are willing, You can make me clean.”
s: Then a leper came to Jesus, begging on his knees: “If You are willing, You can make me clean.”

MRK.1.41.t: Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!”
s: Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!”

MRK.1.42.t: And immediately the leprosy left him, and the man was cleansed.
s: And immediately the leprosy left him, and the man was cleansed.

MRK.1.43.t: Jesus promptly sent him away with a stern warning:
s: Jesus promptly sent him away with a stern warning:

MRK.1.44.t: “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
s: “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

MRK.1.45.t: But the man went out and openly began to proclaim and spread the news. Consequently, Jesus could no longer enter a town in plain view, but He stayed out in solitary places. Yet people came to Him from every quarter.
s: But the man went out and openly began to proclaim and spread the news.
Consequently, Jesus could no longer enter a town in plain view, but He stayed out in solitary places. Yet people came to Him from every quarter.

MRK.2.1.t: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home,
s: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home,

MRK.2.2.t: they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.
s: they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.

MRK.2.3.t: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.
s: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.

MRK.2.4.t: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.
s: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.

MRK.2.5.t: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
s: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”

MRK.2.6.t: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts,
s: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts,

MRK.2.7.t: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
s: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

MRK.2.8.t: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.
s: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.

MRK.2.9.t: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
s: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?

MRK.2.10.t: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,
s: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,

MRK.2.11.t: “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
s: “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

MRK.2.12.t: And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
s: And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”

MRK.4.26.t: Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
s: Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.

MRK.4.27.t: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.
s: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.

MRK.4.28.t: All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.
s: All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.

MRK.4.29.t: And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
s: And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

MRK.4.30.t: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?
s: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?

MRK.4.31.t: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.
s: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.

MRK.4.32.t: But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”
s: But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”

MRK.4.33.t: With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them, to the extent that they could understand.
s: With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them, to the extent that they could understand.

MRK.4.34.t: He did not tell them anything without using a parable. But privately He explained everything to His own disciples.
s: He did not tell them anything without using a parable. But privately He explained everything to His own disciples.

MRK.4.35.t: When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”
s: When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”

MRK.4.36.t: After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.
s: After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.

MRK.4.37.t: Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.
s: Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.

MRK.4.38.t: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”
s: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”

MRK.4.39.t: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
s: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.

MRK.4.40.t: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”
s: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”

MRK.4.41.t: Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”
s: Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”

MRK.5.15.t: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
s: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

MRK.5.16.t: Those who had seen it described what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs.
s: Those who had seen it described what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs.

MRK.5.17.t: And the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.
s: And the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.

MRK.5.18.t: As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him.
s: As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him.

MRK.5.19.t: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”
s: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”

MRK.5.20.t: So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.
s: So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.

MRK.5.21.t: When Jesus had again crossed by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him beside the sea.
s: When Jesus had again crossed by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him beside the sea.

MRK.5.22.t: A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived, and seeing Jesus, he fell at His feet
s: A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived, and seeing Jesus, he fell at His feet

MRK.5.23.t: and pleaded with Him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.”
s: and pleaded with Him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.”

MRK.5.24.t: So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around Him.
s: So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around Him.

MRK.6.1.t: Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples.
s: Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples.

MRK.6.2.t: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?
s: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?

MRK.6.3.t: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.
s: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.

MRK.6.4.t: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”
s: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”

MRK.6.5.t: So He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them.
s: So He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them.

MRK.6.6.t: And He was amazed at their unbelief. And He went around from village to village, teaching the people.
s: And He was amazed at their unbelief.
And He went around from village to village, teaching the people.

MRK.6.30.t: Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.
s: Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.

MRK.6.31.t: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
s: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.

MRK.6.32.t: So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place.
s: So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place.

MRK.6.33.t: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.
s: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.

MRK.6.34.t: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
s: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.

MRK.6.45.t: Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd.
s: Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd.

MRK.6.46.t: After bidding them farewell, He went up on the mountain to pray.
s: After bidding them farewell, He went up on the mountain to pray.

MRK.6.47.t: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.
s: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.

MRK.6.48.t: He could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them,
s: He could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them,

MRK.6.49.t: but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost—
s: but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost—

MRK.6.50.t: for they all saw Him and were terrified. But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
s: for they all saw Him and were terrified.
But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”

MRK.6.51.t: Then He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And the disciples were utterly astounded,
s: Then He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And the disciples were utterly astounded,

MRK.7.31.t: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.
s: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.

MRK.7.32.t: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.
s: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.

MRK.7.33.t: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.
s: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.

MRK.7.34.t: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).
s: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).

MRK.7.35.t: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.
s: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.

MRK.7.36.t: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
s: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.

MRK.7.37.t: The people were utterly astonished and said, “He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”
s: The people were utterly astonished and said, “He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”

MRK.8.1.t: In those days the crowd once again became very large, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called the disciples to Him and said,
s: In those days the crowd once again became very large, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called the disciples to Him and said,

MRK.8.2.t: “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.
s: “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.

MRK.8.3.t: If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.”
s: If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.”

MRK.8.4.t: His disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?”
s: His disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?”

MRK.8.5.t: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied.
s: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked.
“Seven,” they replied.

MRK.8.6.t: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then He took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they distributed them to the crowd.
s: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then He took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they distributed them to the crowd.

MRK.8.7.t: They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well.
s: They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well.

MRK.8.8.t: The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
s: The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.

MRK.8.9.t: And about four thousand men were present. As soon as Jesus had dismissed the crowd,
s: And about four thousand men were present.
As soon as Jesus had dismissed the crowd,

MRK.9.20.t: So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
s: So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.

MRK.9.21.t: Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been with him?” “From childhood,” he said.
s: Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been with him?”
“From childhood,” he said.

MRK.9.22.t: “It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
s: “It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

MRK.9.23.t: “If You can?” echoed Jesus. “All things are possible to him who believes!”
s: “If You can?” echoed Jesus. “All things are possible to him who believes!”

MRK.9.24.t: Immediately the boy’s father cried out, “I do believe; help my unbelief!”
s: Immediately the boy’s father cried out, “I do believe; help my unbelief!”

MRK.9.25.t: When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. “You deaf and mute spirit,” He said, “I command you to come out and never enter him again.”
s: When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. “You deaf and mute spirit,” He said, “I command you to come out and never enter him again.”

MRK.9.26.t: After shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”
s: After shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”

MRK.9.27.t: But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.
s: But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.

MRK.9.33.t: Then they came to Capernaum. While Jesus was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
s: Then they came to Capernaum. While Jesus was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”

MRK.9.34.t: But they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
s: But they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.

MRK.9.35.t: Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all.”
s: Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all.”

MRK.9.36.t: Then He had a little child stand among them. Taking the child in His arms, He said to them,
s: Then He had a little child stand among them. Taking the child in His arms, He said to them,

MRK.9.37.t: “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”
s: “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”

MRK.10.13.t: Now people were bringing the little children to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
s: Now people were bringing the little children to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.

MRK.10.14.t: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
s: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

MRK.10.15.t: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
s: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

MRK.10.16.t: And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them.
s: And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them.

MRK.10.35.t: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”
s: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”

MRK.10.36.t: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.
s: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.

MRK.10.37.t: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”
s: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”

MRK.10.38.t: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”
s: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”

MRK.10.39.t: “We can,” the brothers answered. “You will drink the cup that I drink,” Jesus said, “and you will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.
s: “We can,” the brothers answered.
“You will drink the cup that I drink,” Jesus said, “and you will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.

MRK.10.40.t: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”
s: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”

MRK.10.41.t: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.
s: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.

MRK.10.42.t: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.
s: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

MRK.10.43.t: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
s: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

MRK.10.44.t: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.
s: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.

MRK.10.45.t: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”
s: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

MRK.10.46.t: Next, they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.
s: Next, they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.

MRK.10.47.t: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
s: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

MRK.10.48.t: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
s: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

MRK.10.49.t: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”
s: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.”
So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”

MRK.10.50.t: Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.
s: Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.

MRK.10.51.t: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”
s: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked.
“Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”

MRK.10.52.t: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.
s: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.

NAM.1.3.t: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.
s: The LORD is slow to anger
and great in power;
the LORD will by no means
leave the guilty unpunished.
His path is in the whirlwind and storm,
and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.

NAM.1.4.t: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts.
s: He rebukes the sea and dries it up;
He makes all the rivers run dry.
Bashan and Carmel wither,
and the flower of Lebanon wilts.

NAM.1.5.t: The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away; the earth trembles at His presence— the world and all its dwellers.
s: The mountains quake before Him,
and the hills melt away;
the earth trembles at His presence—
the world and all its dwellers.

NAM.1.6.t: Who can withstand His indignation? Who can endure His burning anger? His wrath is poured out like fire; even rocks are shattered before Him.
s: Who can withstand His indignation?
Who can endure His burning anger?
His wrath is poured out like fire;
even rocks are shattered before Him.

NAM.1.7.t: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress; He cares for those who trust in Him.
s: The LORD is good,
a stronghold in the day of distress;
He cares for those who trust in Him.

NAM.1.8.t: But with an overwhelming flood He will make an end of Nineveh and pursue His enemies into darkness.
s: But with an overwhelming flood
He will make an end of Nineveh
and pursue His enemies into darkness.

NEH.2.1.t: Now in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was set before him, I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had never been sad in his presence,
s: Now in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was set before him, I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had never been sad in his presence,

NEH.2.2.t: so the king said to me, “Why is your face sad, though you are not ill? This could only be sadness of the heart.” I was overwhelmed with fear
s: so the king said to me, “Why is your face sad, though you are not ill? This could only be sadness of the heart.”
I was overwhelmed with fear

NEH.2.3.t: and replied to the king, “May the king live forever! Why should I not be sad when the city where my fathers are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire?”
s: and replied to the king, “May the king live forever! Why should I not be sad when the city where my fathers are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire?”

NEH.2.4.t: “What is your request?” replied the king. So I prayed to the God of heaven
s: “What is your request?” replied the king.
So I prayed to the God of heaven

NEH.2.5.t: and answered the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I ask that you send me to Judah, to the city where my fathers are buried, so that I may rebuild it.”
s: and answered the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I ask that you send me to Judah, to the city where my fathers are buried, so that I may rebuild it.”

NEH.2.6.t: Then the king, with the queen seated beside him, asked me, “How long will your journey take, and when will you return?” So it pleased the king to send me, and I set a time.
s: Then the king, with the queen seated beside him, asked me, “How long will your journey take, and when will you return?” So it pleased the king to send me, and I set a time.

NEH.2.7.t: I also said to him, “If it pleases the king, may letters be given to me for the governors west of the Euphrates, so that they will grant me safe passage until I reach Judah.
s: I also said to him, “If it pleases the king, may letters be given to me for the governors west of the Euphrates, so that they will grant me safe passage until I reach Judah.

NEH.2.8.t: And may I have a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king’s forest, so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel to the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will occupy.” And because the gracious hand of my God was upon me, the king granted my requests.
s: And may I have a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king’s forest, so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel to the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will occupy.”
And because the gracious hand of my God was upon me, the king granted my requests.

NEH.2.11.t: After I had arrived in Jerusalem and had been there three days,
s: After I had arrived in Jerusalem and had been there three days,

NEH.2.12.t: I set out at night with a few men. I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one on which I was riding.
s: I set out at night with a few men. I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one on which I was riding.

NEH.2.13.t: So I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward the Well of the Serpent and the Dung Gate, and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and the gates that had been destroyed by fire.
s: So I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward the Well of the Serpent and the Dung Gate, and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and the gates that had been destroyed by fire.

NEH.2.14.t: Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King’s Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to get through;
s: Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King’s Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to get through;

NEH.2.15.t: so I went up the valley by night and inspected the wall. Then I headed back and reentered through the Valley Gate.
s: so I went up the valley by night and inspected the wall. Then I headed back and reentered through the Valley Gate.

NEH.2.16.t: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews or priests or nobles or officials or any other workers.
s: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews or priests or nobles or officials or any other workers.

NEH.2.17.t: Then I said to them, “You see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned down. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”
s: Then I said to them, “You see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned down. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”

NEH.2.18.t: I also told them about the gracious hand of my God upon me, and what the king had said to me. “Let us start rebuilding,” they replied, and they set their hands to this good work.
s: I also told them about the gracious hand of my God upon me, and what the king had said to me.
“Let us start rebuilding,” they replied, and they set their hands to this good work.

NEH.3.23.t: Beyond them, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs in front of their house, and next to them, Azariah son of Maaseiah, the son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.
s: Beyond them, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs in front of their house, and next to them, Azariah son of Maaseiah, the son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.

NEH.3.24.t: After him, Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and the corner,
s: After him, Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and the corner,

NEH.3.25.t: and Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the angle and the tower that juts out from the upper palace of the king near the courtyard of the guard. Next to him, Pedaiah son of Parosh
s: and Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the angle and the tower that juts out from the upper palace of the king near the courtyard of the guard. Next to him, Pedaiah son of Parosh

NEH.3.26.t: and the temple servants living on the hill of Ophel made repairs opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the tower that juts out.
s: and the temple servants living on the hill of Ophel made repairs opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the tower that juts out.

NEH.3.27.t: And next to them, the Tekoites repaired another section, from a point opposite the great tower that juts out to the wall of Ophel.
s: And next to them, the Tekoites repaired another section, from a point opposite the great tower that juts out to the wall of Ophel.

NEH.3.28.t: Above the Horse Gate, each of the priests made repairs in front of his own house.
s: Above the Horse Gate, each of the priests made repairs in front of his own house.

NEH.4.1.t: Now when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and filled with indignation. He ridiculed the Jews
s: Now when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and filled with indignation. He ridiculed the Jews

NEH.4.2.t: before his associates and the army of Samaria, saying, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Can they restore the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they complete it in a day? Can they bring these burnt stones back to life from the mounds of rubble?”
s: before his associates and the army of Samaria, saying, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Can they restore the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they complete it in a day? Can they bring these burnt stones back to life from the mounds of rubble?”

NEH.4.3.t: Then Tobiah the Ammonite, who was beside him, said, “If even a fox were to climb up on what they are building, it would break down their wall of stones!”
s: Then Tobiah the Ammonite, who was beside him, said, “If even a fox were to climb up on what they are building, it would break down their wall of stones!”

NEH.4.4.t: Hear us, O God, for we are despised. Turn their scorn back upon their own heads, and let them be taken as plunder to a land of captivity.
s: Hear us, O God, for we are despised. Turn their scorn back upon their own heads, and let them be taken as plunder to a land of captivity.

NEH.4.5.t: Do not cover up their iniquity or let their sin be blotted out from Your sight, for they have provoked the builders.
s: Do not cover up their iniquity or let their sin be blotted out from Your sight, for they have provoked the builders.

NEH.4.6.t: So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.
s: So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.

NEH.4.7.t: When Sanballat and Tobiah, together with the Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites, heard that the repair to the walls of Jerusalem was progressing and that the gaps were being closed, they were furious,
s: When Sanballat and Tobiah, together with the Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites, heard that the repair to the walls of Jerusalem was progressing and that the gaps were being closed, they were furious,

NEH.4.8.t: and all of them conspired to come and fight against Jerusalem and create a hindrance.
s: and all of them conspired to come and fight against Jerusalem and create a hindrance.

NEH.4.9.t: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.
s: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.

NEH.5.14.t: Furthermore, from the day King Artaxerxes appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah, from his twentieth year until his thirty-second year (twelve years total), neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.
s: Furthermore, from the day King Artaxerxes appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah, from his twentieth year until his thirty-second year (twelve years total), neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.

NEH.5.15.t: The governors before me had heavily burdened the people, taking from them bread and wine plus forty shekels of silver. Their servants also oppressed the people, but I did not do this because of my fear of God.
s: The governors before me had heavily burdened the people, taking from them bread and wine plus forty shekels of silver. Their servants also oppressed the people, but I did not do this because of my fear of God.

NEH.5.16.t: Instead, I devoted myself to the construction of the wall, and all my servants were gathered there for the work; we did not acquire any land.
s: Instead, I devoted myself to the construction of the wall, and all my servants were gathered there for the work; we did not acquire any land.

NEH.5.17.t: There were 150 Jews and officials at my table, besides the guests from the surrounding nations.
s: There were 150 Jews and officials at my table, besides the guests from the surrounding nations.

NEH.5.18.t: Each day one ox, six choice sheep, and some fowl were prepared for me, and once every ten days an abundance of all kinds of wine was provided. But I did not demand the food allotted to the governor, because the burden on the people was so heavy.
s: Each day one ox, six choice sheep, and some fowl were prepared for me, and once every ten days an abundance of all kinds of wine was provided. But I did not demand the food allotted to the governor, because the burden on the people was so heavy.

NEH.5.19.t: Remember me favorably, O my God, for all that I have done for this people.
s: Remember me favorably, O my God, for all that I have done for this people.

NEH.6.1.t: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and not a gap was left—though to that time I had not yet installed the doors in the gates—
s: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and not a gap was left—though to that time I had not yet installed the doors in the gates—

NEH.6.2.t: Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: “Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono.” But they were planning to harm me.
s: Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: “Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono.”
But they were planning to harm me.

NEH.6.3.t: So I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to go down to you?”
s: So I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to go down to you?”

NEH.6.4.t: Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave the same reply.
s: Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave the same reply.

NEH.8.9.t: Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people said to all of them, “This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep.” For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the Law.
s: Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people said to all of them, “This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep.”
For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the Law.

NEH.8.10.t: Then Nehemiah told them, “Go and eat what is rich, drink what is sweet, and send out portions to those who have nothing prepared, since today is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
s: Then Nehemiah told them, “Go and eat what is rich, drink what is sweet, and send out portions to those who have nothing prepared, since today is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”

NEH.8.11.t: And the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Be still, since today is holy. Do not grieve.”
s: And the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Be still, since today is holy. Do not grieve.”

NEH.8.12.t: Then all the people began to eat and drink, to send out portions, and to rejoice greatly, because they understood the words that had been made known to them.
s: Then all the people began to eat and drink, to send out portions, and to rejoice greatly, because they understood the words that had been made known to them.

NUM.6.22.t: Then the LORD said to Moses,
s: Then the LORD said to Moses,

NUM.6.23.t: “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
s: “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:

NUM.6.24.t: ‘May the LORD bless you and keep you;
s: ‘May the LORD bless you
and keep you;

NUM.6.25.t: may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you;
s: may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you
and be gracious to you;

NUM.6.26.t: may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace.’
s: may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you
and give you peace.’

NUM.6.27.t: So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.”
s: So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.”

NUM.27.12.t: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites.
s: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites.

NUM.27.13.t: After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was;
s: After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was;

NUM.27.14.t: for when the congregation contended in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters.” Those were the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin.
s: for when the congregation contended in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters.” Those were the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin.

NUM.27.15.t: So Moses appealed to the LORD,
s: So Moses appealed to the LORD,

NUM.27.16.t: “May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation
s: “May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation

NUM.27.17.t: who will go out and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd.”
s: who will go out and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd.”

NUM.27.18.t: And the LORD replied to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.
s: And the LORD replied to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.

NUM.27.19.t: Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.
s: Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.

NUM.27.20.t: Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him.
s: Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him.

PHM.1.4.t: I always thank my God, remembering you in my prayers,
s: I always thank my God, remembering you in my prayers,

PHM.1.5.t: because I hear about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints.
s: because I hear about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints.

PHM.1.6.t: I pray that your partnership in the faith may become effective as you fully acknowledge every good thing that is ours in Christ.
s: I pray that your partnership in the faith may become effective as you fully acknowledge every good thing that is ours in Christ.

PHM.1.7.t: I take great joy and encouragement in your love, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of the saints.
s: I take great joy and encouragement in your love, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of the saints.

PHP.1.3.t: I thank my God every time I remember you.
s: I thank my God every time I remember you.

PHP.1.4.t: In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy,
s: In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy,

PHP.1.5.t: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now,
s: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now,

PRO.12.23.t: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, but a foolish heart proclaims its folly.
s: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself,
but a foolish heart proclaims its folly.

PRO.12.24.t: The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
s: The hand of the diligent will rule,
but laziness ends in forced labor.

PRO.12.25.t: Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up.
s: Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man,
but a good word cheers it up.

PRO.12.26.t: A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the ways of the wicked lead them astray.
s: A righteous man is cautious in friendship,
but the ways of the wicked lead them astray.

PRO.12.27.t: A lazy man does not roast his game, but a diligent man prizes his possession.
s: A lazy man does not roast his game,
but a diligent man prizes his possession.

PRO.12.28.t: There is life in the path of righteousness, but another path leads to death.
s: There is life in the path of righteousness,
but another path leads to death.

PRO.13.14.t: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
s: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life,
turning one from the snares of death.

PRO.13.15.t: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.
s: Good understanding wins favor,
but the way of the faithless is difficult.

PRO.13.16.t: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.
s: Every prudent man acts with knowledge,
but a fool displays his folly.

PRO.13.17.t: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
s: A wicked messenger falls into trouble,
but a faithful envoy brings healing.

PRO.13.18.t: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
s: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline,
but whoever heeds correction is honored.

PRO.13.19.t: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.
s: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul,
but turning from evil is detestable to fools.

PRO.13.20.t: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
s: He who walks with the wise will become wise,
but the companion of fools will be destroyed.

PRO.14.12.t: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
s: There is a way that seems right to a man,
but its end is the way of death.

PRO.14.13.t: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.
s: Even in laughter the heart may ache,
and joy may end in sorrow.

PRO.14.14.t: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.
s: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways,
but a good man is rewarded for his ways.

PRO.14.15.t: The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.
s: The simple man believes every word,
but the prudent man watches his steps.

PRO.14.16.t: A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is careless and reckless.
s: A wise man fears and turns from evil,
but a fool is careless and reckless.

PRO.14.17.t: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.
s: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly,
and a devious man is hated.

PRO.14.18.t: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
s: The simple inherit folly,
but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

PRO.15.1.t: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
s: A gentle answer turns away wrath,
but a harsh word stirs up anger.

PRO.15.2.t: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.
s: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge,
but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.

PRO.15.3.t: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
s: The eyes of the LORD are in every place,
observing the evil and the good.

PRO.15.4.t: A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.
s: A soothing tongue is a tree of life,
but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.

PRO.15.28.t: The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.
s: The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer,
but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.

PRO.15.29.t: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.
s: The LORD is far from the wicked,
but He hears the prayer of the righteous.

PRO.15.30.t: The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.
s: The light of the eyes cheers the heart,
and good news nourishes the bones.

PRO.15.31.t: He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
s: He who listens to life-giving reproof
will dwell among the wise.

PRO.15.32.t: He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.
s: He who ignores discipline despises himself,
but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.

PRO.15.33.t: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
s: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom,
and humility comes before honor.

PRO.16.1.t: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.
s: The plans of the heart belong to man,
but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.

PRO.16.2.t: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.
s: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes,
but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.

PRO.16.3.t: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
s: Commit your works to the LORD
and your plans will be achieved.

PRO.16.4.t: The LORD has made everything for His purpose— even the wicked for the day of disaster.
s: The LORD has made everything for His purpose—
even the wicked for the day of disaster.

PRO.16.5.t: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.
s: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD;
be assured that he will not go unpunished.

PRO.16.6.t: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.
s: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for,
and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.

PRO.16.7.t: When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.
s: When a man’s ways please the LORD,
He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.

PRO.16.8.t: Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.
s: Better a little with righteousness
than great gain with injustice.

PRO.16.9.t: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
s: A man’s heart plans his course,
but the LORD determines his steps.

PRO.16.21.t: The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.
s: The wise in heart are called discerning,
and pleasant speech promotes instruction.

PRO.16.22.t: Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.
s: Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor,
but the discipline of fools is folly.

PRO.16.23.t: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.
s: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth
and adds persuasiveness to his lips.

PRO.16.24.t: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
s: Pleasant words are a honeycomb,
sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.

PRO.16.27.t: A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.
s: A worthless man digs up evil,
and his speech is like a scorching fire.

PRO.16.28.t: A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.
s: A perverse man spreads dissension,
and a gossip divides close friends.

PRO.16.29.t: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.
s: A violent man entices his neighbor
and leads him down a path that is not good.

PRO.16.30.t: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.
s: He who winks his eye devises perversity;
he who purses his lips is bent on evil.

PRO.16.31.t: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
s: Gray hair is a crown of glory;
it is attained along the path of righteousness.

PRO.16.32.t: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
s: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior,
and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.

PRO.17.9.t: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
s: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love,
but he who brings it up separates friends.

PRO.17.10.t: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
s: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment
deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.

PRO.17.11.t: An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
s: An evil man seeks only rebellion;
a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

PRO.17.12.t: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
s: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs
than a fool in his folly.

PRO.17.13.t: If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
s: If anyone returns evil for good,
evil will never leave his house.

PRO.17.14.t: To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
s: To start a quarrel is to release a flood;
so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.

PRO.17.15.t: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
s: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous—
both are detestable to the LORD.

PRO.17.16.t: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
s: Why should the fool have money in his hand
with no intention of buying wisdom?

PRO.17.17.t: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
s: A friend loves at all times,
and a brother is born for adversity.

PRO.17.22.t: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
s: A joyful heart is good medicine,
but a broken spirit dries up the bones.

PRO.17.23.t: A wicked man takes a covert bribe to subvert the course of justice.
s: A wicked man takes a covert bribe
to subvert the course of justice.

PRO.17.24.t: Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
s: Wisdom is the focus of the discerning,
but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.

PRO.17.25.t: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him.
s: A foolish son brings grief to his father
and bitterness to her who bore him.

PRO.17.26.t: It is surely not good to punish the innocent or to flog a noble for his honesty.
s: It is surely not good to punish the innocent
or to flog a noble for his honesty.

PRO.17.27.t: A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.
s: A man of knowledge restrains his words,
and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.

PRO.17.28.t: Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.
s: Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent,
and discerning when he holds his tongue.

PRO.18.10.t: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
s: The name of the LORD is a strong tower;
the righteous run to it and are safe.

PRO.18.11.t: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.
s: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city;
it is like a high wall in his imagination.

PRO.18.12.t: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
s: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud,
but humility comes before honor.

PRO.18.19.t: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
s: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city,
and disputes are like the bars of a castle.

PRO.18.20.t: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.
s: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled;
with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.

PRO.18.21.t: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
s: Life and death are in the power of the tongue,
and those who love it will eat its fruit.

PRO.18.22.t: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
s: He who finds a wife finds a good thing
and obtains favor from the LORD.

PRO.18.23.t: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.
s: The poor man pleads for mercy,
but the rich man answers harshly.

PRO.18.24.t: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
s: A man of many companions may come to ruin,
but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.

PRO.19.1.t: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
s: Better a poor man who walks with integrity
than a fool whose lips are perverse.

PRO.19.2.t: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
s: Even zeal is no good without knowledge,
and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.

PRO.19.3.t: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
s: A man’s own folly subverts his way,
yet his heart rages against the LORD.

PRO.19.20.t: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
s: Listen to counsel and accept discipline,
that you may be wise the rest of your days.

PRO.19.21.t: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
s: Many plans are in a man’s heart,
but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.

PRO.19.22.t: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.
s: The desire of a man is loving devotion;
better to be poor than a liar.

PRO.19.23.t: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.
s: The fear of the LORD leads to life,
that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.

PRO.20.5.t: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.
s: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters,
but a man of understanding draws them out.

PRO.20.6.t: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?
s: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion,
but who can find a trustworthy man?

PRO.20.7.t: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.
s: The righteous man walks with integrity;
blessed are his children after him.

PRO.20.9.t: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?
s: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure;
I am cleansed from my sin”?

PRO.20.10.t: Differing weights and unequal measures — both are detestable to the LORD.
s: Differing weights and unequal measures —
both are detestable to the LORD.

PRO.20.11.t: Even a young man is known by his actions— whether his conduct is pure and upright.
s: Even a young man is known by his actions—
whether his conduct is pure and upright.

PRO.20.12.t: Ears that hear and eyes that see— the LORD has made them both.
s: Ears that hear and eyes that see—
the LORD has made them both.

PRO.21.29.t: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright man makes his way sure.
s: A wicked man hardens his face,
but the upright man makes his way sure.

PRO.21.30.t: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD.
s: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel
that can prevail against the LORD.

PRO.21.31.t: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
s: A horse is prepared for the day of battle,
but victory is of the LORD.

PRO.22.1.t: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.
s: A good name is more desirable than great riches;
favor is better than silver and gold.

PRO.22.2.t: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.
s: The rich and the poor have this in common:
The LORD is Maker of them all.

PRO.22.3.t: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.
s: The prudent see danger and take cover,
but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.

PRO.22.4.t: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.
s: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD
are wealth and honor and life.

PRO.22.5.t: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; he who guards his soul stays far from them.
s: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse;
he who guards his soul stays far from them.

PRO.22.22.t: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,
s: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor,
and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,

PRO.22.23.t: for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who rob them.
s: for the LORD will take up their case
and will plunder those who rob them.

PRO.22.24.t: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,
s: Do not make friends with an angry man,
and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,

PRO.22.25.t: or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.
s: or you may learn his ways
and entangle yourself in a snare.

PRO.22.26.t: Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.
s: Do not be one who gives pledges,
who puts up security for debts.

PRO.22.27.t: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
s: If you have nothing with which to pay,
why should your bed be taken from under you?

PRO.24.15.t: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy his resting place.
s: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous;
do not destroy his resting place.

PRO.24.16.t: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times.
s: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up;
but the wicked stumble in bad times.

PRO.24.17.t: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,
s: Do not gloat when your enemy falls,
and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,

PRO.24.18.t: or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him.
s: or the LORD will see and disapprove,
and turn His wrath away from him.

PRO.24.19.t: Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.
s: Do not fret over evildoers,
and do not be envious of the wicked.

PRO.24.20.t: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
s: For the evil man has no future;
the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

PRO.24.23.t: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
s: These also are sayings of the wise:
To show partiality in judgment
is not good.

PRO.24.24.t: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”— peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him;
s: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”—
peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him;

PRO.24.25.t: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come upon them.
s: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty,
and rich blessing will come upon them.

PRO.24.26.t: An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips.
s: An honest answer given
is like a kiss on the lips.

PRO.25.1.t: These are additional proverbs of Solomon, which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:
s: These are additional proverbs of Solomon, which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:

PRO.25.2.t: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out.
s: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter
and the glory of kings to search it out.

PRO.25.3.t: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings cannot be searched.
s: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep,
so the hearts of kings cannot be searched.

PRO.25.4.t: Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth.
s: Remove the dross from the silver,
and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth.

PRO.25.5.t: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
s: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence,
and his throne will be established in righteousness.

PRO.25.11.t: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
s: A word fitly spoken
is like apples of gold in settings of silver.

PRO.25.12.t: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.
s: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold
is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.

PRO.25.13.t: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters.
s: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest
is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him;
he refreshes the soul of his masters.

PRO.25.14.t: Like clouds and wind without rain is the man who boasts of gifts never given.
s: Like clouds and wind without rain
is the man who boasts of gifts never given.

PRO.25.25.t: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
s: Like cold water to a weary soul
is good news from a distant land.

PRO.25.26.t: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.
s: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well
is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.

PRO.25.27.t: It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory.
s: It is not good to eat too much honey
or to search out one’s own glory.

PRO.25.28.t: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper.
s: Like a city whose walls are broken down
is a man who does not control his temper.

PRO.26.17.t: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
s: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears
is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.

PRO.26.18.t: Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows,
s: Like a madman shooting firebrands
and deadly arrows,

PRO.26.19.t: so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
s: so is the man who deceives his neighbor
and says, “I was only joking!”

PRO.26.20.t: Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.
s: Without wood, a fire goes out;
without gossip, a conflict ceases.

PRO.26.21.t: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
s: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire,
so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.

PRO.26.22.t: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
s: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels
that go down into the inmost being.

PRO.27.1.t: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
s: Do not boast about tomorrow,
for you do not know what a day may bring.

PRO.27.2.t: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth— a stranger, and not your own lips.
s: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth—
a stranger, and not your own lips.

PRO.27.5.t: Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed.
s: Better an open rebuke
than love that is concealed.

PRO.27.6.t: The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
s: The wounds of a friend are faithful,
but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

PRO.27.7.t: The soul that is full loathes honey, but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.
s: The soul that is full loathes honey,
but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.

PRO.27.8.t: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who wanders from his home.
s: Like a bird that strays from its nest
is a man who wanders from his home.

PRO.27.9.t: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is counsel to the soul.
s: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart,
and the sweetness of a friend is counsel to the soul.

PRO.27.10.t: Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend, and do not go to your brother’s house in the day of your calamity; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
s: Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend,
and do not go to your brother’s house
in the day of your calamity;
better a neighbor nearby
than a brother far away.

PRO.27.11.t: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me.
s: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart,
so that I can answer him who taunts me.

PRO.27.12.t: The prudent see danger and take cover; but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
s: The prudent see danger and take cover;
but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.

PRO.27.13.t: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
s: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger;
get collateral if it is for a foreigner.

PRO.27.14.t: If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.
s: If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning,
it will be counted to him as a curse.

PRO.27.15.t: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike—
s: A constant dripping on a rainy day
and a contentious woman are alike—

PRO.27.16.t: restraining her is like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.
s: restraining her is like holding back the wind
or grasping oil with one’s right hand.

PRO.27.17.t: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
s: As iron sharpens iron,
so one man sharpens another.

PRO.27.23.t: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds;
s: Be sure to know the state of your flocks,
and pay close attention to your herds;

PRO.27.24.t: for riches are not forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.
s: for riches are not forever,
nor does a crown endure to every generation.

PRO.27.25.t: When hay is removed and new growth appears and the grain from the hills is gathered,
s: When hay is removed and new growth appears
and the grain from the hills is gathered,

PRO.27.26.t: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.
s: the lambs will provide you with clothing,
and the goats with the price of a field.

PRO.27.27.t: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you— food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants.
s: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you—
food for your household
and nourishment for your maidservants.

PRO.29.8.t: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
s: Mockers inflame a city,
but the wise turn away anger.

PRO.29.9.t: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.
s: If a wise man goes to court with a fool,
there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.

PRO.29.10.t: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.
s: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man,
but the upright care for his life.

PRO.29.11.t: A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.
s: A fool vents all his anger,
but a wise man holds it back.

PRO.31.1.t: These are the words of King Lemuel—the burden that his mother taught him:
